The Calamity SNOTEL reported 22 inches of snowfall.
Snow showers increased the night of the 25th, continuing through the 26th, resulting in significant travel issues for the holiday weekend. Around 5 to 10 inches of snowfall were reported.

A prolonged winter weather event occurred across the Pacific Northwest during the Christmas holiday, resulting in significant travel issues across the coast range. Several SNOTELs reported 14 to 28 inches of snow through the period.
Spotters reported 4 to 6 inches of snowfall.

Landslides dumped mud, trees, and rocks across Highway 126 about 10 miles east of Florence. An estimated 300 yards of the highway was covered by the landslide, which took about 24 hours to clear.

Rain and snow showers occurred overnight, with clearing skies and temperatures dipping to or below freezing in the morning. A vehicle, carrying high school students on their way to school, slid and crashed into a fence and a house around 8am in the morning.
Strong south winds were reported along the south Washington coast with sustained winds between 35 and 55 mph with a peak gust to 69 mph at Cape Disappointment (82SW1).

Strong south winds were reported along the north Oregon coast with sustained winds between 45 and 55 mph with a peak gust to 77 mph at Garibaldi (GARO3.)  Around 2030PST tree branches were reported by ODOT over highway 26 near Necanicum resulting in traffic delays.

Strong south winds were reported along the central Oregon coast with maximum sustained winds between 35 and 75 mph. A peak gust of 86 mph occurred on the Yaquina Bay Bridge (ODT38).  There was a downed tree and powerlines over highway 229 near Kernville at 2300PST.

The seas at buoy 46029 (20NM West of Columbia River Mouth) rose to 26 feet at 11 seconds which would bring high surf conditions to the coastline. High Surf conditions continued at times through 1/3/2022 at 1640PST, then seas gradually subsided.

The seas at buoy 46029 (20NM West of Columbia River Mouth) rose above 26 feet at 11 seconds which would bring high surf conditions to the coastline. High Surf conditions continued at times through 1/3/2022 at 1640PST, then seas gradually subsided.

The worst flooding in a number of years (over a decade per the Emergency Manager) in the Tokeland area. Water level made it up to the Tokeland Hotel.  In the Raymond area, a 1/2 miles stretch of Highway 101 was closed, and 7 homes in the Peter St and Sherman Avenue reported flooding.  During this time high seas and high river levels in the area contributed to the flooding.  As a result, the tide peaked at 13.4 feet around 1230PST at the Tokeland tide gauge.

During this time high seas and high river levels in the area contributed to the flooding.  As a result, the tide peaked around 12.5 feet around 1300PST at the Astoria tide gauge.  This event ranked #1 for highest tides at the Astoria and Cape Disappointment tide gauges, 12.5 feet and 11.8 feet (MLLW) respectively.

The seas at buoy 46050 (20NM West of Newport, OR) rose above 24 feet at 11 seconds which would bring high surf conditions to the coastline. Seas peaked at 30 feet at 12 seconds on 1/3/2022 at 1940PST. High Surf conditions continued at times through 1/3/2022 at 0540PST, then seas gradually subsided.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: Strong south winds were reported in the Central Coast Range with maximum sustain winds around 40 mph with a peak gust of 96 mph at Cape Perpetua (AV549).  Near Deadwood, dozens of limbs snapped off Alder trees and dozens of conifers uprooted along Indian Creek Road.  In addition, over a dozen trees had fallen across North Fork Siuslaw road between Brickerville and Minerva.

The gauge on the Marys River near Philomath rose above flood stage of 20 feet around 0920PST, crested at major flood stage of 21.0 feet at 1500 PST, then dropped below flood stage on the 5th at 0340PST.
The gauge on the Luckiamute River near Suver rose above flood stage of 27 feet at 0900PST, crested at 27.2 feet at 1315PST, then dropped below flood stage at 2020PST.

Highway 126 at Cushman was closed due to high water caused by a combination of high tide of 11.9 feet as measured at the South Beach tide gauge, and rising of the Siuslaw river due to recent heavy rain.  This event ranked #2 for highest tide at the Garibaldi tide gauge.
A debris flow from the Tumalt Creek drainage blocked all lanes of I-84, a major transportation corridor between western and eastern Oregon.
The gauge on the Nehalem River near Foss rose above flood stage of 15.0 feet at 1300PST, crested at 18.3 feet on the 7th at 0830PST, then dropped below flood stage on the 8th at 1220PST.

The gauge on the Wilson River near Tillamook rose above flood stage of 12.0 feet at 0945PST, crested at 14.1 feet on the 7th at 0800PST, then dropped below flood stage at 1730PST on the 7th.  Flood waters covered highway 101 near Tillamook, and highway 6 was closed in east Tillamook near Goodspeed Park.
The gauge on the Luckiamute River near Suver rose above flood stage of 27.0 feet at 1230PST, crested at 27.6 feet on the 7th at 1000PST, then dropped below flood stage on the 8th at 0900PST.
Tillamook county emergency manager reported large debris flow on Trask River Road at milepost 6. Mud, large rocks and trees blocking all lanes.
Road failure during heavy rain closed Oregon highway 202 approximately 1 mile southeast of Olney.
Oregon highway 47 near the Mist junction was closed due to a culvert failing, washing out the road.

The gauge on the Grays River near Rosburg rose above flood stage of 12.0 feet at 0640PST, crested at 16.2 feet on the 7th at 0200PST, then dropped below flood stage on the 8th at 0340PST.  In addition to river flooding, widespread areal flooding resulted in a lot of road closures in the county, trapping people for 3 days.

The gauge on the Naselle River near Naselle rose above flood stage of 15.0 feet on the 6th, crested at 18.3 feet at 2000PST. This is above major flood stage of 17.0 feet. The river then dropped below flood stage on the 7th at 1130PST.

The gauge on the Willapa River near Willapa rose above flood stage of 21.0 feet at 1620PST, crested at 23.3 feet on the 7th at 0345PST (major flood stage is 24.0 feet), then dropped below flood stage on the 7th at 1750PST.  As a result, 33 homes have significant damage (combined river and coastal flooding.) Two people were sheltered. Also landslides preventing road entries into the county including five slides on SR 105.

The gauge on the Cowlitz River at Kelso rose above flood stage of 21.5 feet at 1330PST, crested at 24.0 feet at 2130PST, the dropped below flood stage on the 7th at 2300PST.  There were reports of several side road closed due to flood waters.

The gauge on the Grays River near Rosburg rose above flood stage of 12.0 feet at 2345PST, crested at 15.5 feet on the 12th at 0715PST, the fell below flood stage at 2330PST.   A mudslide closed SR-4 in both direction near Raistakka Road.

A tsunami generated by an eruption of the Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'api volcano reached the U.S. West coast.  A tsunami wave height of 0.2 feet was measured at the Astoria tide gauge on the 15th. No reports of damage or injury are known at this time.

A tsunami generated by an eruption of the Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'api volcano reached the U.S. West.  A tsunami wave height of 0.7 feet was measured at the Newport tide gauge on the 15th. No reports of damage or injury are known at this time.

A tsunami generated by an eruption of the Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'api volcano reached the U.S. West coast.  The tsunami wave height of 0.5 feet was measured at the Westport tide gauge. No reports of damage or injury are known at this time.

Strong south wind of 38 mph with a peak gust of 71 mph was reported by the Trout Creek RAWS (TCFO3).

A very active frontal system brought heavy snow to the South Washington Cascades on the 2nd and 3rd with snow totals between 17 and 27 inches. Peak snow fall rates are estimated at 3 to 4 inches per hour. One particular site, June Lake SNOTEL (MRBW1) at 3440 feet had 34 inches.
A very active frontal system brought heavy snow to the South Washington Cascade Foothills on the 2nd and 3rd with snow totals from 8 to 14 inches.

A very active frontal system brought heavy snow to the Northern Oregon Cascades on the 2nd and 3rd with snow totals mostly between 21 and 29 inches. Peak snow fall rates are estimated at 3 to 4 inches per hour. One particular site, Bear Grass SNOTEL (BKSO3) at 4720 feet had 34 inches snowfall. Another site, Red Hill SNOTEL (REDO3) at 4410 feet received 18 inches of snow in 6 hours, on the 3rd between 0200PST to 0800PST. US-20 over Santiam Pass was closed due to heavy snow.
A very active frontal system brought heavy snow to the Northern Oregon Cascades Foothills on the 3rd with snow totals of 11 to 15 inches.

A very active frontal system brought heavy snow to the Cascades in Lane County on the 3rd and 4th with snow totals mostly between 21 and 26 inches. One site, McKenzie SNOTEL (MKZO3) at 4770 feet had a total of 32 inches of snow.
A very active frontal system brought heavy snow to the Cascade Foothills in Lane County on the 3rd and 4th. Railroad Overpass SNOTEL (RROO3) at 2680 feet had a snow total of 7 inches.

Heavy snow and ice accumulation resulted in the closure of I-84, a major transportation corridor connecting western and eastern Oregon and Washington.  Around 24 inches of snow fell in Stevenson, WA.  In the Multnomah Falls area along I-84, 5 inches of snow fell with an unknown amount of ice accumulation, leading to the highway closure.

events.cz_name: CASCADE HEAD TO FLORENCE...10 TO 60 NM
events.event_narrative: Coast Guard Sector North Bend received a mayday call at approximately 0000PDT Saturday (3/26/2022) from the Captain of the Ship, Morgan, of the White Swan III  reporting that his vessel was sinking in the north end of the Heceta Banks fishing area. Morgan also reported that a female crew member was aboard the vessel. The 13th Coast Guard District Command Center received an emergency position indicating radio beacon alert from the White Swan III. Upon arrival at the scene of the EPIRB location, an MH-65 Dolphin rescue helicopter crew from Air Facility Newport spotted a debris field and a life raft. The aircrew had to return to base due to heavy fog and low visibility. Seas started out near 6 to 8 feet according to Buoy 46050 through the majority of Friday (3/25/2022). Winds at this time where also well below Small Craft criteria.  Seas looked to fluctuate between 9 to 10 feet until 1100PDT Saturday. Winds also gusted at times around 21 to 22 kt through the same time period.  Visibility during the previous day (3/25/2022) was down to 1 statue mile at the Florence airport K6S2 for part of the day.
The Yaquina Bridge sensor (ODT38) reported sustained winds of 47 mph gusting to 63 mph.

Eugene Public Utility District reported about 1600 customers without electrical power in the Pleasant Hill, Dexter, Cottage Grove and Cloverdale areas. The fallen tree also hit a house near the bridge. A daily record rainfall was recorded at Portland International Airport of 1.42 inches on the 10th.

The Multnomah County Medical Examiner reported suspected deaths associated with the heat wave. One each on July 25th, 26th, 27th; two each on the 28th and 30th, all in Portland. A man drowned on the Sandy River on the 27th while paddle boarding. During the heatwave there were elevated numbers of heat related illnesses. For example on the 30th, Multnomah County reported 10 requests for Emergency/Urgent care. A typical summer day is zero to one. There was a cumulative of 63 heat illness, more than half of a typical summer. In another incident on July 25th, a man drowned while swimming at Henry Hagg Lake in Washington County.  Also in Washington County, a dog died from the heat when left in a car. Other suspected heat related deaths occurred July 28th and 29th in Clackamas County.
Four suspected heat related deaths occurred in Marion county.

Lightning started an estimated 20 to 30 wildfires in the Willamette National Forest in early August.  The Cedar Creek Fire started on the morning of the 1st. The fire grew to around 7800 acres by the end of the month.  Impacts included smoke settling in the Oregon 58 corridor affecting the towns of Oakridge and Westfir.

Seaside Lifeguards and Seaside Fire & Rescue rescued a total of 16 swimmers who got caught up in rip currents at Seaside and Cannon Beach over the weekend.   A man in his 50s was found unconscious in the water near Seaside Saturday afternoon, but efforts to revive him were not successful.

The Cedar Creek Fire continued to burn through the month, growing to approximately 120,700 acres with 27 percent containment at the end of the month.  The fire grew considerably on the 9th-10th when dry east winds hit the area. On the 9th, Level 3 (Go Now) evacuation notices were posted for the Oakridge, Westfir, and High Prairie communities.

The fire started on the afternoon of the 9th and was extinguished by the afternoon of the 10th. In all 30 acres were burned, 15 of which was in the park itself. One home and a barn were destroyed.  Around 550 homes near the park were evacuated.  No injuries were reported.  Oregon Department of Forestry and Estacada Fire Department has not determined the cause of the fire.

The Vitae Springs Fire started in South Salem Friday evening and was fully contained by late Saturday morning.  The estimated burned area is around 165 acres, mostly in dense brush and wooded areas, including in steep terrain. Approximately 119 single-family homes were in the Level 3 (Go Now) evacuation zone. There were no reported injuries or structure losses due to the fire.

The Siouxon Fire, caused by an abandoned campfire, was reported on the 22nd. It grew to around 306 acres by the end of the month. The fire was primarily in the Siouxon Creek drainage in the southwest corner of the Gifford Pinchot National Forest, in remote hard to reach area which was previously impacted by the 2020 Big Hollow Fire and is uncontained.

Dense fog developed early in the morning, with an inversion in place and enhanced by wildfire smoke in the area. Around 60 to 65 vehicles piled up on I-5 southbound, roughly 20 miles north of Eugene, near Harrisburg, in Linn County. At least one confirmed dead, and four others taken to the hospital. I-5 was closed for many hours. Six of the vehicles leaked fluids on the roadway triggering a HAZMAT response.

A brief, weak tornado occurred on Saturday evening northeast of Cherryville, OR. Video confirmation was obtained, as well as a storm damage survey.  It did cause damage to trees, powerlines, a vehicle, one residence, and small outbuildings. Estimated wind speeds of 75 to 85 mph which rates this tornado as EF-0.

A weak tornado occurred in rural Woodburn, confirmed by video and supported by damage photos obtained from the public. Rated EF-0 with winds estimated between 61-74 mph. Damage to two residential properties.
The Cedar Creek Fire continued to burn through the month, growing to approximately 127,283 acres with 60 percent containment by October 27th.

Heavy rains over an approximately 2 year old burn area (Riverside Fire) triggered a debris flow. This is reportedly to have occurred sometime on November 5th. The debris flow crossed Highway 224 at the junction with Indian Henry Road, near a bridge crossing the Clackamas River. A nearby rain gauge had 3.31 inches in the 24 hours ending 1700PST November 5th.

In addition to recent heavy rain, wind gusts as high as 43 mph resulted in tree damage and power outages in the area. Snow began falling around 0430 PST with significant accumulations around 0800 PST, then tapering off around 0800 PST on the 14th. A total of 4 to 8 inches fell. Around 3 to 7 inches of snow was common along the Coast Range, with up to 10 inches at Saddle Mountain at 3110 feet elevation.

Light snow began to around 0900 PST, but the heaviest snow fell during the afternoon through early evening hours. Around 6 to 12 inches of snow fell in the Portland/Vancouver metro area by 2230 PST. This resulted in snarled traffic and numerous traffic accidents. Many vehicles were caught up in the traffic jam well into the night.  Portland International Airport closed briefly.  Schools and government offices were closed for up to two days following the event. Over 80 Trimet buses were stranded due to the rapidly deteriorating road conditions. Hundreds of cars were abandoned on area roadways, even on freeways.

Halfway through the race, police think the man veered off the course, and his body was later found in a nearby field.  He was quoted as being healthier than a horse, and police said weather likely contributed to his death.

No one was with the man when he collapsed, but help was called for when he was found. Emergency workers could not revive him. The Yamhill County Sheriff's Office said it appeared he had no water with him, and heat could have contributed to his death.

A man fell into Johnson Creek and drowned. Moderate to heavy rainfall December 2nd through 3rd produced bank full conditions and swift moving water in the creek.

Blizzard-like conditions were observed at the height of the storm with roughly 1 to 4 inches of a snow/sleet across the Portland and Vancouver metro area and widespread east wind gusts of 35-55 mph. This led to hundreds of downed trees and limbs, resulting in widespread and extended power outages. Multnomah County, the City of Portland, City of Lake Oswego declared a State of Emergency. Portland Parks and Recreation reported 380 downed trees or large branches, The City of Lake Oswego reported more than 100 downed trees. These reports along with trees downed on private property, at least 500 trees were downed in the Portland Metro area.  Downed trees and power lines resulted in power outages. Portland General Electric had a peak count of 165,000 customers without power. Portland Bureau of Transportation had 29 road closures due to downed powerlines and trees within the city of Portland, TriMet cancelled all public transportation. Additional roads were closed across Washington and Multnomah Counties including parts of Highway 30 and US 26. At least 10 homes and 25 cars were damaged from downed trees. Damage estimates are from counties of Multnomah & Clackamas which have boundaries outside the NWS zone. There was no cost estimate from Washington county for this report.||There were 7 direct fatalities due to either suspected hypothermia, falling objects. Two indirect fatalities attributed to a generator used to warm an apartment caught fire. Another indirect fatality occurred when a tree fell on a RV, starting a fire killing one of two occupants. Three direct injuries occurred when a tree fell on a tent injuring the occupants.
Minor flooding occurred on the Luckiamute River near Suver as an atmospheric river brought heavy rains.
Heavy rain produced minor flooding along the Siletz River at Siletz. The river crested at 17.7 feet at 6 pm on December 5th. Flood stage is 16.0 feet.

A strong atmospheric river brought heavy rains to the north Oregon coast on Dec 5th. Tillamook County EM reported Kilchis River just north of Tillamook had minor flooding. The Wilson River at Tillamook also remained in minor flood stage during a 30-hour period, cresting at 16.07 feet at 330 pm on December 5th. Flood stage is 12.0 feet. The Trask River also rose above minor flood stage, cresting at 17.0 feet at 10 pm on December 5th. Flood stage is 16.5 feet. Rockaway Beach in southern Tillamook County had localized flooding due to heavy rain. Manzanita in northern Tillamook County had a power outage probably due to downed trees on power lines. Miami Foley Road was washed out which put Highway 101 as the only direct route between Garibaldi and Mohler.

Heavy rain produced minor flooding along the Cowlitz River at Kelso. The river crested at 22.10 feet at 12 pm on December 6th. Flood stage is 21.5 feet.||A landslide also occurred on the 503 Spur Road which cut off the community of Cougar in Cowlitz County.

EF-0 tornado with estimated winds of 85 mph. The tornado briefly touched down in Rockaway Beach, OR. It occurred around 9:24 PM 11/11/24 and lasted one to two minutes or so according to the spotter that reported it. KRTX radar imagery depicted a fairly strong velocity couplet over Rockaway Beach. This likely formed as a waterspout then made landfall, though the path was not continuous. There were multiple reports of damage to fences, roof shingles, and a window and dirt/debris being tossed around. Upon further investigation, more security camera video footage was received from the Neah-Kah-Nie School district showing distinct rotation of a tornado moving through a parking lot where several items were thrown or moved including portions of a baseball dug-out, porta-potty, and several dumpsters. A garage on the premises had its roof blown off and the garage doors blown in. One minor injury was reported. The maximum width of the the tornado is estimated at 150 yards and an estimated path length of 0.25 miles based on damage reports.

The fire covered nearly 8,000 acres, located about 11 miles north of Trout Lake, and spanned between both Skamania and Yakima counties in the Gifford Pinchot National Forest.
A lightning strike damaged electrical and computer equipment at a sewage treatment plant, causing a back-up in sewage treatment and discharge, as well as extensive damage.
Lightning struck the Walt Morey Middle School, damaging some of the computer systems.
Firefighters responded to a greenhouse fire, which had been struck by lightning. The greenhouse was completely destroyed, but the nearby home was saved.

A Multnomah County Medical Examiner reported that a man died from hyperthermia on Feb 2 in the 97219 ZIP code. The morning temperatures were around 35 degrees Fahrenheit with light precipitation and calm winds. It is unclear whether the death was due to the temperatures from this day or a prolonged exposure to cold as the overnight temperatures were around 25 degrees from January 25 through 30.

The offshore marine buoy 46029 reported 23 to 34 ft swells from the afternoon on Feb 24 through the afternoon on Feb 25. The high surf resulted in the United States Coast Guard closing the Columbia River Bar to marine traffic for almost 24 hours. This is a financial loss as 63 million dollars worth of commerce moves across the Columbia River Bar per day.

Drone footage posted on the Lane County Facebook page showed flooding of pastures, farms, roads, and homes in Mohawk Valley.

Heavy persistent rainfall resulted in localized flooding at several of Eugene parks and creeks impacting Alton Baker Park, Delta Ponds, and along the Fern Ridge Path. A trained spotter reports lots of ponding of water near Fairmount Blvd and E 19th Ave, downhill from Hendricks Park. Additionally, another trained spotter reports parts of Amazon Park Trail underwater in the area of E 23rd Ave and Willamette St. due to small stream/river flooding.
Due to heavy rainfall a Trained Spotter reported small stream flooding with water on Hendricks Rd near Enterprise Rd.

There were multiple photos on Facebook showing flooded of pasture land, roads, and a building along and near Latham Rd. A Social Media post showed a picture of flooding across Bennet Creek Rd. There was also another Social Media Post showing a couple of feet of water in the parking lot up to the Horners Inc building in north Cottage Grove.
Received pictures from the public via email of a funnel cloud near Mount Angel the morning of April 21st. MRMS indicated weak/shallow convection in the area around the time of the report.
Photographs and video from social media, in addition to a special METAR from KEUG, indicate a funnel cloud developed around 1-2 miles northwest of the Eugene Airport.

A landspout was photographed and briefly recorded to the west-northwest of Central Linn High School in the fields around Halsey, OR. No damage was reported. A small condensation funnel was observed above the ground circulation by the observer even though the photographs and video did not show the condensation funnel.  The ground circulation and condensation funnel were not visibly connected. Time is based on the public report. Location and path width are roughly estimated based on video footage.

There were two fatalities presumed heat related of a Male, 59 in the 97233 zip code and a Female, 58 in 97214 zip code. Emergency managers and health officials reported elevated Multnomah County 911 calls due to the heat and higher than normal hospital/urgent care heat related visits.

There were a couple of fatalities presumed to be due to the Heat with a Male, 56, in 97209 zip code, and a Female, 55 (Clackamas County). Additionally there were reported elevated County 911 calls due to the heat and elevated hospital/urgent care heat related visits for both Multnomah county and Clackamas county.

A Utility partner shared webcam imagery of a funnel cloud that appeared to last for around ten minutes with a thunderstorm that moved east-northeastward between McMinnville, OR and Unionvale, OR. Based on the webcam imagery alone, there are no clear signs of debris being lofted or wind damage occurring at the surface.

Broadcast media reported a funnel cloud associated with a strong rain shower around 3:53 PM PDT Oct. 12, 2025 in La Center, Washington. There were no reports of a tornado on the ground and/or wind damage with this cell.

The NWS Damage Assessment Team surveyed wind damage from a strong convective shower that moved through Longview, Washington around 3:13 PM PDT Oct. 12, 2025. Based on the wind damage, estimated peak winds of 80-85 mph occurred, most likely with a wet microburst that produced damaging straight-line winds over a small geographic area.

Additional a 60mph peak gust was measured at the Astoria-Megler Bridge mesonet station at 1743 PST. This station was at or near warning criteria 1300 to 1930 PST. It's worth noting the Pacific County Emergency Manager estimated around $60,000 dollars worth of damage was produced from this storm.

events.event_narrative: A member of the public posted to social media a video of a faint but distinguishable water spout just off the coast of Ocean Park, WA via Facebook.

A person was walking on the sand near the mouth of Siletz Bay when a sneaker wave knocked them off of their feet and dragged them into the ocean.  Once in the water, a strong rip current quickly swept them out to sea. They were swept out far enough that the people on the beach could not see them. The person did not survive, and their body was found on the beach around 4 miles south from where they were swept in. The 3 pm buoy observation from buoy 46050 reported a west swell of 11ft with a 16 second period.

The Wilson River Hwy., or OR Hwy. 6, was closed for a time period due to a mudslide that covered the highway, about 15 miles east of Tillamook.  Heavy rains in the Coast Range which contributed to the flooding of the Wilson River also triggered the mudslide.

Trask River Road at milepost 7.5 was reported closed due to high water.  The was caused by the heavy rain that fell over the Coast Range, that resulted in the flooding of the Trask River.  A woman driving a car was stuck in the high water along the road, but was rescued.

Flooding due to heavy rain in the Coast Range caused multiple closures along Hwy. 101 north of and inside downtown Tillamook.  The flooding also affected local businesses along the highway, where flood waters in some places were near two feet high. NOTE: Damage estimate is for the entire Tillamook county.

Heavy rains over the Willapa Hills drained into the Grays River, raising the river out of it's banks. This combined with high tides brought flooding to areas in Wahkiakum county, especially around the town of Rosburg.  Flooding in the area closed local roads as well as some evacuations of people from their homes.

Heavy rain draining into local rivers, including the Trask River and nearby Tillamook River, caused local flooding.  Flooding along Fawcett Creek, which drains into the Tillamook, washed out a bridge along S. Prairie Road. Two vehicles containing 8 people total had to be rescued from the rushing water after trying to cross the washed out bridge. No major injuries were reported.

events.event_narrative: Between 11 and 24 inches of snow fell in the north Oregon Coast Range based on spotter reports, road reports and snotel data.
Nine to 10 inches of snow fell in the Lower Columbia region of northwest Oregon. Trained spotters in Clatskanie reported 10 inches of snow.

Fourteen to 24 inches of snow fell across the northern Willamette Valley. Some reports include 14 inches in Canby, 18 inches in Gladstone, 21 inches in Oregon City and 24 inches in Wilsonville.  This storm was the most significant storm to hit the Portland Metro area in the past 40 years.  Freezing rain also occurred during this period with 1/4 to 3/4 inch of ice accumulation.

Ten to 20 inches of snow fell across the central Willamette Valley. Some reports include 10 inches in McMinnville, 17 inches in Dundee and 20 inches in Lafayette.  Freezing rain also occurred during this storm, which produced 1/4 to 1/2 inch of ice accumulation.  This snowfall combined with accumulations from the previous few days resulted in 3 roof collapses and 10 carport collapses.  The heavy snow also downed several dozen tress in the Enchanted Theme Park causing significant damage.
Eighteen to 48 inches of snow fell across the north Oregon Cascade Foothills.  Some reports include 19 inches in the Bull Run watershed and 48 inches in Rhododendron.
Eighteen to 20 inches of snow fell across the Lane County Cascade Foothills.  Some reports include 18 inches in the communities of Oakridge and McKenzie Bridge.

A tornado was reported by the public to local television station KVAL in Eugene. NWS Storm Survey visited the residence and confirmed: a small shed-like structure was lifted off the ground and blown 21 feet to the east - counter to the prevailing storm winds.  There were also circular carvings in the grass nearby.

A report called in by a former spotter, strong gusty winds brought numerous trees down along Hwy. 22.  Other reports from this storm included wind gusts strong enough to snap Cottonwood tree branches estimated at 10 to 12 inches in diameter along Hwy. 214.

NWS Storm Survey visited a site with extensive damage most likely the result straight-line thunderstorm winds.  Numerous large tree branches ranging in diameter of 10 to 16 inches snapped off of several trees.  The wind speed is estimated from damage in a nearby county under similar conditions.
At the Portland WFO, strong wind gusts knocked down a small tree in the parking lot, as well as snapped off a large branch from a different tree on the property.

Outside of Chapters Books and Coffee in Newberg, a tree with estimated diameter 10 to 12 inches was snapped in half. Also, numerous spotter reports just to the north and  with similar conditions were reported.

The top of a 70-foot tree, estimated between 20 and 20 inches in diameter, was snapped off in downtown Portland at the intersection of SW Salmon Street and Park Avenue.  A passer-by was nearly hit as it fell to the ground.  Time of the event is estimated based nearby reports from the storm.
A park ranger on the Sisi Butte lookout tower reported heavy rain accompanied by hail of various sizes, the largest estimated to be 3/4 of an inch.

A funnel cloud was sighted and photographed north of Brownsville during the afternoon.  The time and exact location are estimated based on the narrative from the newspaper clipping.  The funnel cloud and another one nearby never touched the ground, lasted only a few minutes before they disappeared.

A media television station in Eugene, OR, KVAL, reported a member of the public called them with a report of a funnel cloud, and sent a photo to the station.

Strong wind gusts were recorded on the Yaquina Bay Bridge.  Strong winds were also reported at Lincoln City, with a gusts up to 70 kt, and at Gleneden Beach, with sustained winds up to 41 kt.
Strong winds were recorded at Toke Point.
Strong winds were reported at Toke Point.  Peak winds of 56 knots were also reported in Oysterville and Ocean Park.  A crab boat on Willapa Bay also reported 78 knot winds.

Strong winds were reported in Oysterville.  Other locations reported strong winds, including: Toke Point with  sustained winds up to 48 kt and gusts to 64 kt; a spotter in Ocean Park with gusts to 57 kt; Long Beach with gusts to 50 kt; and a crab boater reported winds gusts to 79 kt on the Willapa Bay.

Strong winds were reported by a spotter in Salmon Creek. He also reported many trees down in his neighborhood, including on his home, which verified other reports by broadcast media of similar conditions bringing damage to private property around Vancouver.

Strong winds were reported at the airport in Hoquiam, and are representative of the zone.  Strong winds were also reported in the Willapa hills by the NWS WSR-88D Doppler Radar in the range of 60-70 kt at radar level.  There were power outages reported in Kalama due to branches bringing down power lines, which is just upstream of the southwest Washington interior.

Strong winds were reported in Garibaldi.  Strong winds were also reported at many other stations, including: Warrenton with a peak wind gust of 50 kt; Astoria with a peak wind gust of 68 kt on the Megler Bridge; Clatsop Spit with a gust to 73 kt. Roof damage to the Seaside City Hall was reported, as well as power outages throughout the city. Trees were reported down along portions of US Hwy. 101 in Cannon Beach.

Strong wind gusts were reported on Hwy 101 in Tillamook on the Yaquina Bay Bridge.  Strong winds were also reported in other areas along the coast, including: a peak wind gust of 59 kt in Lincoln City; sustained winds of 48 kt with a wind gust to 85 kt by a spotter in downtown Newport, where siding damage was also reported; wind gust to 83 kt by a spotter in Waldport, where a satellite dish was reportedly ripped off a fence.

Strong winds were reported at Mt. Hebo, with more frequent gusts reaching 56 kt.  Additionally, NWS WSR-88D Doppler radar reported winds between 60 and 70 kt at radar level.  Timing was estimated when winds reached the surface based on elevated reports and radar.

The uprooted trees were about 20-24 inches in diameter, and one was carried 20 yards downwind.  One home had major roof damage, with 40-50% of the roof collapsed.
A funnel cloud was reportedly spotted over McNary Feild in Salem, but stayed aloft and never touched down.  NWS WSR-88D Doppler radar indicated many convective showers around the area.

Two fishermen were reported missing late Wednesday night when they did not return from a fishing trip.  Coast Guard searched for the men both on land and sea, but the search was called of late Thursday.  Both high winds and rough seas were occurring at the time due to an incoming storm.

The Scott Mountain Fire was started by lightning on Thursday, August 19, 2010. The fire burned 3464 acres in the Mt. Washington Wilderness and the National Forest managed by the McKenzie River Ranger District. The fire was contained by mid-September.

Hood and Willamette National Forests. The fires began on Tuesday, August 17, 2010 and burned 4775 acres before being contained near the end of September.

Damage reports along the path of the tornado include destruction of a greenhouse, a large storage canopy with PVC frame destroyed, several trees with diameter of 6-8 inches snapped off or blown down, several tree branches of 1-4 inches in diameter broken off and a metal roof blown off a barn.

Lone Pine SNOTEL measured 18 inches of new snow. Sheep Canyon SNOTEL and June Lake SNOTEL also received 18 inches of new snow.

events.event_narrative: Strong winds were reported at Mary's Peak with wind gusts to 70 kt.
Strong winds were reported at Sugarloaf RAWS with wind gusts to 66 kt.
A funnel cloud was observed near Finley NWR. It lasted nearly 3 minutes.
A funnel cloud was observed in SE Harrisburg. The funnel cloud lasted 8 minutes.
A funnel cloud was observed near the Hillsboro airport. The funnel cloud lasted for approximately 5 minutes.

A tornado touched down near the intersection of 14th St. and NE Kirby St. in McMinnville Oregon. Several 8-10 inch diameter trees were snapped at this location. The tornado continued Southeast for one block through a residential neighborhood with some tree damage noted. The tornado lifted a camper and deposited it over a chain link fence in a nearby industrial area and lofted 300 pound trellises. This damage was consistent with EF1 wind speeds. The tornado dissipated as it moved Southeast of 11th Ave and Lafayette. Some straight line wind damage was noted at a nearby park after this time.

A funnel cloud was observed about 2 miles WNW of the Portland International airport. The observer estimated that it extended 200 to 300 feet below the cloud base. The funnel cloud lasted approximately 5 minutes.
A 54 year-old Vancouver woman died after being caught in a rip current near Lincoln City. Two other swimmers were able to swim back to shore.
Two people were rescued from the D River Wayside near Lincoln City, Oregon. Shortly after this rescue, three more people were rescued from rip currents at Roads End Park near Lincoln City.
Heavy rain and hail caused debris to cover part of the access road between Government Camp and the Timberline Lodge. The hail size was estimated.
Ten or more trees down including one snapped 15 to 20 ft above ground level. Most of these were on side of the highway.
Spotter estimated hail size of 0.88 inch.
Strong wind gusts blew several shingles off of a roof near Marion Bridge.
A thunderstorm produced 1.5 inch diameter hail on Highway 26 around 3 miles west of Government Camp.
Maximum winds measured at Garibaldi NOS (TLB03) of 48 mph gusts 64 mph. Wind gusts to 69 mph were also measured at Clatsop Spit (3CL03).
Wind speeds of 43 mph gusts 56 mph were measured at Yaquina Bridge (ODOT), 44 mph gust 52 mph at Newport C-Man, and a peak gust of 64 mph at Yachats.
Winds in the valley were 30 to 40 mph. These winds brought a tree down onto a house in SE Portland and left around 5000 people without power. Most of the power outages were in Washington County.
Strong winds were reported at Cape Disappointment with sustained winds of 46 mph and gusts to 61 mph.

Strong winds were reported at Garibaldi with sustained winds of 60 mph and gusts to 75 mph. Strong winds were also reported at Clatsop Spit with sustained wind of 48 mph and gusts to 61 mph, and at TIlamook with a gust to 58 mph.

Strong winds were reported at Mt. Hebo with gusts to 66 mph. Strong winds were also reported at Tidewater RAWS with a peak gust of 66 mph.

Media reported via social media that a tree fell onto a mobile home near Hillsboro. Another social media report poted a picture of a tree that fell on two cars at the Fred Meyer in Oak Grove There was other reports of several large trees down around the Portland Metro Area. Portland General Electric reported over 25,000 customers were without power in Clackamas and Multnomah counties.
Strong winds were reported at Cape Disappointment with sustained wind of 52 mph and gusts to 61 mph.
Strong winds were reported with sustained wind of 63 mph and gusts to 90 mph on Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) tower near Naselle.
Strong winds were reported at Cape Disappointment with sustained wind of 46 mph and gusts to 59 mph.
Strong winds were reported at Naselle Ridge with sustained wind of 59 mph and gusts to 81 mph.

Strong winds were also reported at Clatsop Spit with sustained wind of 44 mph and gusts to 55 mph, and a peak gust of 59 mph was measured at the Astoria Airport. The Oregon Department of Transportation reported a downed tree and tree debris on Highway 101 near Cloverdale.

Strong winds were reported at Lincoln City with a measured gust of 72 mph. Strong winds were also reported at the Yaquina Bay Bridge with a gust of 66 mph, and at Newport with sustained winds of 40 mph.

Strong winds were reported at Mt. Hebo with a measured gust of 61 mph. Strong winds were also reported at Tidewater RAWS with sustained wind of 39 mph and gusts to 69 mph. The Oregon Department of Transportation reported that several trees and tre debris were on Highway 26 near Elsie.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: Strong winds were reported at Mary's Peak BPA with sustained 51 mph and gusts to 85 mph. The Oregon Department of Transportation reported a downed tree and tree debris blocked lanes on Highway 101 near Gardiner.
Strong winds were reported at Sugarloaf RAWS with peak gusts to 79 mph.
A tree hit by lightning fell and damaged two homes in Aloha.
Around 4 inches of rain fell over the Willapa Hills, and resulted in the Grays River near Rosburg to exceed flood stage.
A total of 9.54 inches was measured at Rock Creek from September 28, 2013 through September 30, 2013 which caused local flooding.
Around 7 inches of rain fell for the North Oregon Coast from September 28, 2013 to September 30, 2013 resulting in the Wilson River near Tillamook to exceed Flood Stage.

KPTV-KPDX Broadcasting reported that heavy rain resulted in flooding and damage to the Legacy Good Samaritan Medical Center and several businesses in Northwest Portland. Besides damage to the hospital's emergency and operating room, some elective surgeries were cancelled.
A measured sustained wind of 44 mph with gusts to 68 mph was reported at the Abernathy RAWS (ABNW1).
A sustained wind of 45 mph was measured at Cape Disappointment (82SW1) with a gust of 53 mph.

A NWS Spotter estimated Winds of 55 mph, and reported several trees down along Highway 47 between Banks and Forest Grove. They reported power lines down and power outages in the area. A local media station KOIN stated that Pacific Power reported 12,500 customers without power in Northeast Portland for several hours. KOIN also said that Concordia University cancelled their morning classes. PG&E reported that there were 2800 customers without power in Clackamas County.

Sustained winds of 44 mph was measured at the NOS Garibaldi (TLB03) station with gusts up to 59 mph. Similar winds were measured for the Megler Bridge on US 101 (ODT76), Clatsop Spit (3CLO3), and Pacific City (AT297). The peak gust at Pacific City was 65 mph.

A peak gust of 62 mph was measured at US 101 Yaquina Bridge (ODT65). The C-Man Station at Newport (NWP03) measured sustained winds of 41 mph with a gust of 51 mph. The highest wind measurement was a peak gust of 67 mph at Lincoln City (AR659).
Sustained winds of 45 mph were measured at US 101 Megler Bridge(ODT76) with a gust of 58 mph. Cape Disappointment (82SW1) had a wind gust of 53 mph with a maximum sustained wind of 44 mph.

An 88 year old woman wandered from her nursing home, became disoriented, and died outdoors. The Cowlitz County Coronor ruled the cause of death Hypothermia. The media reported temperatures of 28 degrees early Friday. Mesonet stations in Longview reported a minimum temperaure of 25 degrees at station AP806 and 27 degrees at LOPW1.

NWS Spotters, Emergency Managers, the media and the general public reported 4 to 9 inches of snow in the South Willamette Valley. The highest amounts of 8 to 9 inches were measured in Corvallis, Philomath, and Creswell.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: NWS Spotters, local media, Emergency Managers, and the general public reported 6 to 9 inches of snow in the Central Willamette Valley. Snow totals of 6 to 9 inches were reported in Veneta, Lorane, Philomath, Creswell, and Swisshome.

The weather station at Government Camp (GOV50) reported temperatures between -2 and 2 degrees with sustained winds of 22 mph. The peak gust was 60 mph. These values resulted in -20 to -30 degree Fahrenheit wind chills. The temperature and wind at Tombstone Pass (ODT50) calculated to wind chills of -15 to -25 degrees Fahrenheit.

Temperature and Winds at The Oregon Department of Transportation weather station at Willamette Pass calculated to -20 degrees Fahrenheit. There is uncertainty on the ending time of this event because the wind sensor failed on the 7th.

The temperature and wind from the Bonneville Power Administration's weather station at Augspurger Mountain calculate to wind chills of -15 to -25 degrees Fahrenheit.  Temperatures were as low as 3 degrees with east winds 20 mph with gusts to 40 mph.
A barn near Dallas Oregon was heavily damaged by wind gusts, and a few trees and tree branches were broken. These trees took down some power lines. A Storm Survey estimated gusts of 55 mph.
Clatsop Spit recorded sustained winds of 43 mph with gusts to 54 mph.
Twenty inches of snow was measured at June lake (3340 feet). A snow rate of 1 inch per hour was measured around 1900 PST on January 11th.

Two USGS weather stations near Mount Hood reported heavy snow. One was at Timberline (TIM60) around 6000 feet where 21 inches was measured between 0600 PST January 11 to 1000 PST January 12. The 1 inch per hour criteria was met at 0600 PST (January 11th). The other station is at Mount Hood Measows (MHM52) at 5200 feet where 15 inches of snow was reported between 1900 PST on January 11th and 1000 PST January 12. The 1 inch per hour criteria was met here at the onset of the snow (January 11 at 1900 PST).

Heavy snow was determined for the Lane County Cascades by the Roaring River SNOTEL station (ROR03) at 4900 feet where 15 inches of snow was measured between 0800 PST January 11th through 0400 PST January 12th. The 1 inch per hour criteria was met at 1600 PST on January 11th.
Freezing rain impacted the upper hood river valley area with two reports from the public of ice accumulations around 0.25 inch just northwest of Parkdale on Trout Creek Road (1500 feet elevation).
A trained Spotter reported around 0.10 inch of ice accumulation around Hood River.

Strong winds were reported at several weather stations along the South Washington Coast including 55mph sustained winds with a gust of 79 mph at Megler Bridge (ODT76). Cape Disappointment (82sW1) also measured a peak gust of 70 mph, with Toke Point (TOKW1) measuring sustained winds of 40 mph and a gust of 56 mph.
The Abernathy RAWS (ABNW1) reported sustained winds of 41 mph with a peak gust of 67 mph.

Many weather stations along the North Oregon coast reported High Winds with the strongest winds reported at Megler bridge (ODT76) with sustained winds of 55 mph, and a peak gust of 79 mph. The high winds were reported from Tillamook to Astoria and average around 45 mph sustained with 70 mph gusts.

Many weather stations reported high winds along the Central Oregon Coast from Newport to Gleneden Beach. The highest gust was 76 mph reported at Gleneden Beach (C9821). Generally sustained winds of 40 mph with gusts around 60 mph were observed.
The Tidewater RAWS (MTR03) measured Sustained winds of 46 mph with a peak gust of 72 mph.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Rockhouse RAWS (RKH03) measured sustained winds of 47 mph with a peak gust of 74 mph.

Strong East winds tipped a semi-trailer over while traveling across the Glen Jackson Bridge on January 23rd. This accident resulted in traffic delays on Interstate 205 and closed boat traffic for just over an hour. Additional winds on January 24th resulted in the collapse of a carport at a Vancouver apartment complex. Over 2000 Clark Power Utility customers lost power for around an hour due to downed tree limbs on power lines.

Strong east winds resulted in knocking two large trees over. One of these trees came down on a SUV in Milwaukie, and the other came down on an SUV in southwest Portland. There were also 100s of people without power for at least an hour due to downed limbs on power lines.

Many weather stations reported high winds along the North Oregon Coast. A few of the more noteworthy measurements include a gust of 82 mph with sustained winds of 55 mph at Megler Bridge (ODT76), and sustained winds of 56 mph with a gust to 70 mph at Garibaldi NOS (TLB03).

Many weather stations reported high winds along the Central Oregon Coast. A few of the more noteworthy measurements include a gust of 76 mph with sustained winds of 45 mph at Yachats (E1135), and a gust to 70 mph at Lincoln City (AR659). High winds were reported from Yachats to Lincoln City. There were reports of downed trees including damage to two automobiles.
The Tidewater RAWS (MTR03) measured sustained winds of 43 mph with a peak gust of 67 mph. There was also a police report of trees blocking Highway 26 at mile marker 36 near the Vernonia Junction.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Rockhouse RAWS (RKH03) reported sustained winds of 40 mph with a peak gust of 69 mph. Wind gusts of 91 mph were reported at the Mary's Peak. The media also reported that there were several trees down due to the winds.
Strong winds downed a few trees and damaged a vehicle in Gresham.

Three weather stations along the South Washington Coast measured strong winds as a Pacific storm system moved onshore. Cape Disappointment (82SW1 measured a peak gust of 66 mph, Toke Point NOS (TOKW1) measured a gust of 59 mph, and Megler Bridge (ODT76) measured a peak gust of 82 mph.

Two weather stations reported strong winds in the Southwest Washington Coast Range. The Abernathy RAWS (ABNW1) reported sustained winds of 44 mph with a peak gust of 65 mph, and Naselle Ridge (BPNAS) measures a maximum wind of 92 mph.
Strong winds were measured at Megler Bridge (ODT76) with sustained winds of 56 mph and a gust of 70 mph. Cape Disappointment (82SW1) measured sustained winds of 49 mph and a peak gust of 62 mph.

Two stations measured strong wind gusts in the Southwest interior. A peak gust of 64 mph was measured at the Abernathy RAWS (ABNW1), and a gust of 86 mph was measured at the Naselle Ridge BPA Observing Station (BPNAS).

Several weather stations along the entire North Oregon coast measured high winds on February 15, 2014. The strongest wind gust was 86 mph which was measured at Garibaldi NOS (TLB03). Pacific City (AT297), Megler Bridge (ODT76), and Clatsop Spit (3CLO3) measured peak wind gusts between 69 and 72 mph. A spotter in Tillamook reported a wind gust of 65 mph, and the Astoria Airport measured a peak gust of 60 mph. Cannon Beach (D4535) reported a peak gust of 58 mph. Sustained winds were also high at Garibaldi (61 mph) and Megler Bridge (56 mph).

Fourteen weather stations along the Central Oregon Coast measured high winds on February 15, 2014. The strongest wind gust was 93 mph which was measured at Sea lion Caves. Yaquina bridge (ODT38) and Gleneden Beach had peak gusts of 78 mph. Highways 18, 101, and 20 had partial closures due to tree debris.
High winds was reported at the Tidewater RAWS (MTR03) with sustained winds of 38 mph and a peak gust of 67 mph. Highways 26 and 53 were closed due to downed trees blocking the roads.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: Two weather stations reported high winds in the Central Oregon Coast range with the strongest wind gust of 86 mph reported from the BPA station at Mary's Peak (BPMAR). The other verifying observation was sustained winds of 39 mph and a peak gust of 64 mph from the Rockhouse RAWS (RKHO3).

Two weather stations along the South Washington Coast measured high winds on February 16, 2014. Cape Disappointment (82SW1) measured high winds for 6 hours with a peak gust of 69 mph, and Megler Bridge measured sustained winds of 56 mph with a peak gust of 71 mph.

The Southwest Washington coast range including the Willapa Hills experienced high winds February 16th, 2014. The Abernathy RAWS (ABNW1) measured sustained winds of 39 mph with a peak gust of 58 mph, and the BPA station at Naselle Ridge measured a peak gust of 91 mph.

The weather station at Garibaldi (TLB03) measured 9 hours of high winds, with sustained winds of 51 mph and a peak gust of 66 mph. Clatsop Spit (3CLO3) measured 5 hours of high winds and also had a peak gust of 66 mph. Pacific City (AT297) and Rockaway Beach (AS469) also verified high winds for the coast with a peak wind of 58 mph and 64 mph respectively.

Lincoln City (AR659) and the Yaquina Bridge (ODT38) measured peak winds of 62 mph on February 17th. Yachats (AS531) showed a brief period of high winds around 0500 PST and reported a peak gust of 58 mph.

Two stations in the Northwest Oregon Coast Range measured high winds. The Hebo BPA weather station reported 11 hours of high winds with a peak gust of 63 mph, and the Tidewater RAWS (MTRO3) measured sustained winds of 35 mph with a peak gust of 61 mph.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: Two weather stations reported high winds in the Central Oregon Coast range. The Rockhouse RAWS (RKHO3) measured sustained winds of 37 mph between 0200 PST and 0600 PST with a peak gust of 60 mph. The BPA station at Mary's Peak measured a peak gust of 74 mph.

Two stations along the South Washington Coast reported high winds on February 18th. Cape Disappointment (82SW1) measured sustained winds of 40 mph with a peak gust of 51 mph, and Megler Bridge (ODT76) measured sustained winds of 47 mph with a peak gust of 57 mph.
The Abernathy RAWS (ABNW1) reported a peak gust of 59 mph between 1330 PST and 1600 PST.
Megler Bridge (ODT76) reported sustained winds of 47 mph with a peak gust of 57 mph, and the weather station at Garibaldi (GARO3) measured sustained winds of 41 mph.

Several stations reported high winds along the Central Oregon Coast on February 18, 2014. Some of the more noteworthy observations were a peak wind of 65 mph reported at Lincoln City (AR659) and sustained winds of 48 mph measured at the Yaquina Bridge (ODT38).

Strong and gusty east winds through the Columbia River Gorge resulted in impacts around the Portland metro area. Local media reported that a large tree fell onto a Max train and overhead wires in Gresham that closed that line for the rest of the day. Another downed tree crushed a SUV in Lake Oswego. A large tree took out power lines as it fell across Highway 43, disrupting power and closing the highway for a couple of hours. A Large tree branch fell and pierced through a window of a van that was driving on Highway 99 with luckily no injuries.
The Grays river at Rosburg reached flood stage at 150 AM PST. The river level crested at 13.2 feet at 545 AM PST, and fell below flood stage at 100 PM PST.
The Siuslaw River near Mapelton reached flood stage at 440 PM PST on February 12, 2014, and crested near 18.02 feet at 500 PM PST. The river dropped below flood stage at 530 PM PST on February 12th.
The Mohawk River near Springfield reached flood stage at 400 PM PST. The river crested at 15.1 feet at 515 PM PST, and fell below flood level at 630 PM PST.
The Pudding River at Aurora reached flood stage at 1130 AM on February 16th 2014. The river crested at 22.4 feet at 500 AM on February 17th, and fell below flood level at 930 AM PST on February 18th.
The Nehalem River near Foss reached Flood Stage at 720 AM PST on February 17th, 2014. The river crested at 14.5 ft at 900 AM, and dropped below flood level at 200 PM PST.
The Nehalem River near Foss reached flood stage at 1220 PM PST on February 18th, 2014. The river crested at 15.1 feet at 615 pm PST, and dropped below flood level at 800 AM PST on February 19, 2014.

A report on a social media network from the Oregon State Police News reported a fatality indirectly related to high surf at the North Jetty in Florence, OR. The time of the accident occurred at 5:55 pm which was around 3 hours after a High Surf Advisory had expired. Water rushing up the beach swept three family members that were sitting on a large log away from the log. One of the victims tried to help an elderly family member up from being knocked down by the water when the log estimated to be 40 ft long and 25 inches in diameter rolled over him. The man sustained fatal injuries from being struck by the log.

Biddle Butte gusted greater than 35 mph with a peak gust of 60 mph, and a CWOP station in Washougal (AP164) frequently gusted to 25 mph with a peak of 44 mph. There were no snow reports with in this snow, but snow reports near by support that 4 to 8 inches of snow in the area. Near by Cascade Locks reported 8 inches of snow.

Corbett was gusting greater than 35 mph with a peak gust to 60 mph. There were no snow reports in this zone, but near by reports suggests that there was 4 to 8 inches of snow. Cascade Locks reported 8 inches of snow.

A 30-mile wide band of heavy snow set up along the Oregon coast in the morning on the 6th, and resulted in 4 to 8 inches of snow from Tillamook to Manzanita. The heaviest snowfall reports reported was 8 inches from a NWS spotter in Manzanita and 7 inches from a public report at Rockaway Beach.

Snow in the morning along the Central Oregon coast changed into freezing rain in the afternoon before ending with 2 to 4 inch snow accumulations. The greatest snowfall reported was 4 inches in Waldport. There was 2 inches of snow in Newport followed with a quarter of an inch of ice.

Heavy snow on the Northern Oregon Coast range with the greatest amount of 13 inches 6 miles northwest of Vernonia. That snow was reported by a Ham operator. There were two snow reports from ODOT stations with 10 inches of snow (Wilson River Summit and Sunset Summit).

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: Snow began early in the morning for the Central Oregon coast Range then changed to freezing rain later in the morning and rain in the afternoon. There was a report by the public of 6 inches of snow in Alsea.

Light snow started early in the morning then increased during the afternoon resulting in a winter weather advisory being upgraded to a warning. A couple more noteworthy reports include one from the general public of 8.5 inches in Scappoose, and an ODOT report of 7 inches of snow in Clatskanie.

Snowfall totals varied across the Portland metro area ranging from 2 to 9 inches with the highest amounts near Hillsboro and Scappoose. A report from the general public of 8.5 inches of snow for Scappoose. There were two HAM Amateur radio reports of 6 inches of snow for Hillsboro and Gresham. Portland received 3 to 4 inches of snow which was reported from various sources including NWS employees, Trained spotters and the NWS office.

The Central Willamette Valley was in between two heavier bands of snow to their north and to their south and generally had less snow than other areas in NW Oregon. However, a couple of locations still met the Winter Weather Warning criteria including 5 inches of snow 8 miles northwest of Newberg and 4 inches at Monmouth.

Snow came fast and furious into the South Willamette Valley and continued heavy at times throughout the day. Most locations saw 5 to 10 inches of snow. The highest measured snow amounts follow. Two trained spotters reported 11.5 inches of snow at Corvallis and 9.3 inches of snow at Philomath. A public report provided 9 inches in Albany, and an amateur HAM radio operator relayed 7 inches of snow in Halsey.

There were no snow observations from within this zone, but heavy snow in near by Detroit (1500 feet elevation) confirms there was heavy snow in the Oregon Cascade Foothills. A trained spotter reported 14 inches of snow in Detroit and ODOT reported 9 inches of snow. Therefore, it is estimated that there was 7 to 15 inches of snow in the foothills.
The Hood River County Emergency Manager reported 10 inches of snow in Hood River. The Oregon Department of Transportation reported 9 inches in Hood River and 8 inches in Cascade Locks.

There were two reports of heavy snow in Parkdale. One from the Hood River County Emergency Manager who reported 14 inches of snow, and the other from the Oregon Department of Transportation who reported 10 inches.

Light snow began early in the morning, then increased during the afternoon resulting in a Winter Weather Advisory being upgraded to a Winter Weather Warning. A person from the gernal public reported 7 inches of snow in Woodland, and two trained NWS spotters reported 6 inches of snow at Kalama and Longview.

A band of Heavy snow moved through Clark County, with heavier snow early in the day than the rest of the Greater Portland/Vancouver metro area. Snow accumulations were generally 5 to 9 inches. A blogger reported 9.5 inches of snow in Ridgefield, and we received a Facebook post of 7.5 inches of snow in Salmon Creek. A HAM amateur radio operator repoted 7 inches of snow in Battle Ground.

Although there were no reports on the Washington side of the Central Columbia River Gorge there were several reports of heavy snow in the more populated areas just across the River in Oregon. The Hood River County Emegency Manager reported 10 inches of snow in hood River. The oregon Department of Transportation reported 9 inches of snow in Hood River, and 8 inches in Cascade Locks. With these observations it is estimated that 7 to 12 inches of snow fell on the Washington side of the Central Columbia River Gorge.
A NWS Trained Spotter reported reported 4 inches of snow in Tillamook. This was in addition to the around 4 inches of snow that fell on the previous day (February 6th).

There was generally 1 to 4 inches of accumulating snow with the heaviest amounts south of downtown Portland. A CoCoRaHs observer reported 7 inches of snow in Greston, a NWS Employee reported 5.5 inches of snow in Oregon City, a person from the general public reported 4 inches in West Linn, and another NWS employee reported 3.8 inches of snow in SW Portland/Garden Home.
A mix of snow and ice produced 3 inches of snow in Siletz and 0.25 inch of ice in Newport.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: Generally 5 to 8 inches of snow fell in the Central Oregon Coast Range, gradually changing to ice in some of the valleys before ending. Someone from the general public reported 14 inches of new snow at Mary's Peak. Another person from the public reported 5 inches of snow in Alsea followed by light icing. A trained spotter reported 7 inches of snow in Blodgett followed by 0.5 inch of ice.

A mix of snow and ice produced 11.2 inches of snow 1.5 miles west of Timber. This snow was followed by 0.25 inch of ice. This wintery precipitation was in addition to the 10 to 12 inches of snow that fell on February 6th.

Generally 3 to 6 inches of snow fell in the Central Willamette Valley. The precipitation changed to sleet briefly then to freezing rain late in the event. The Oregon State Police warned not to travel on Interstate 5 between Salem and Eugene due to the icy roadways. Some snow reports include 6 inches of snow in Salem, Turner and Aumsville. There was also 6 inches of snow in Dallas that was followed by 0.25 inch of ice. McMinnville measured 5 inches of snow, with Yamhill close behind at 4.5 inches.

Generally 5 to 9 inches of new snow fell in the Southern Willamette Valley. The snow eventually changed to sleet briefly, then freezing rain downing tree limbs and power lines. The Oregon State Police warned not to travel on Interstate 5 between Salem and Eugene due to the icy roadways. Power outages started to develop which continued to increase as the next event (Ice Storm Warning 1) developed on its heels.
A trained spotter reported 8.5 inches of snow in Detroit. This is in addition to the 9 to 14 inches of snow that fell in the area on the previous day, February 6th.

There were few reports from the warning area but the Oregon State Police recommended against travel south of Eugene on Interstate 5 due to snow and ice. Snow eventually changed to ice, and power outages started to develop as the next event (Ice Storm Warning 1) developed. By 2300 PST, The Oregon Department of Transportation reported road closures near Cottage Grove due to downed trees and limbs from the weight of the ice. From nearby reports it is estimated that there was 4 to 8 inches of snow and 0.25 inch of ice.

There are limited reports during this event, but based on reports of 4 inches in Parkdale and 9 inches in BZ Corner, and early reports of 1 to 2 inches of snow in the Gorge and Hood River at the beginning event, estimate that 4 to 9 inches of new snow fell. There were also intermittent closures of Interstate 84 due to snow and icy roads.

There are limited reports during this event, but based on reports of 4 inches in Parkdale and 9 inches in BZ Corner, and early reports of 1 to 2 inches of snow in the Gorge and Hood River at the beginning event, estimate that 4 to 9 inches of new snow fell. There were also intermittent closures of Interstate 84 due to snow and icy roads.

Based on radar and nearby reports, 6 to 12 inches  of snow were followed by 0.25 to 0.5 inch of ice, leading to numerous downed trees and power outages. A media meteorologist reported 0.5 inch of ice in his weather blog for Corbett. There were several reports from the Oregon Department of Transportation of Black Ice on the roads.

An Oregon Department of Transportation weather station on Megler Bridge reported high winds for 17 hours with a maximum sustained winds of 50 mph and a peak gust of 72 mph. Another station at Cape Disappointment measured high winds for around 12 hours with maximum sustained winds of 48 mph and a peak gust of 62 mph.
The Abernathy RAWS (ABNW1) measured high winds for 2 hours early in the aftrnoon on March 6,2014 with a peak gust of 62 mph.

Several weather stations reported high winds for the North Oregon Coast with many locations gusting above 57 mph for 15 to 17 hours. Some of the more noteworthy winds include a 72 mph gust at Megler Bridge and a 71 mph gust at Garibaldi. Pacific City reported a peak gust of 69 mph, and both the Astoria ASOS and Tillamook AWOS reported peak gusts around 60 mph.

Several weather stations reported high winds along the Central Oregon Coast with many locations reported wind gusts greater than 57 mph for 16 consecutive hours. The highest wind gust was 71 mph at Lincoln City with the second highest a 68 mph at Yaquina Bridge, and then a 67 mph gust in Yachats. Newport and Waldport both measured a peak gust of 58 mph.
The Tidewater RAWS measured sustained winds of 40 mph with a peak gust of 63 mph. Winds at this station gusted above 57 mph for 12 consecutive hours.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Rockhouse RAWS measured sustained winds of 40 mph with a peak gust of 76 mph. High winds with gusts greater than 57 mph were measured for 12 consecutive hours.

Strong winds resulted in significant damage in the Portland Metro Area with area wind measurements between 30 and 48 mph. There were several reports of 12 to 24 inch diameter trees down. One landed on the Firestone Tire Building downtown Portland, one closed a busy intersection at Hall and Bonita in Tigard, and another closed 'A' Avenue downtown Lake Oswego. There were numerous power outages where tens of thousands of PGE customers were without power. Clackamas Community College cancelled all classes on March 6 due to the power outages.

A burst of winds took down a large tree that destroyed a deck, trampoline,and shed. The supports of the shed were said to have shoved 3 feet into the ground. Nearby weather stations reported measured wind gusts between 33 and 43 mph.
Weather stations at Clatsop Spit and Megler bridge measured peak wind gusts of 63 mph for around 5 consecutive hours on March 8.
The Tidewater RAWS measured wind gusts around 66 mph for an hour in the afternoon on March 8.
The Oregon Department of Transportation's weather station on Yaquina Bridge measured sustained winds of 45 mph for an hour in the afternoon on March 8.

The Oregon Department of Transportation's weather station on Megler Bridge measured sustained winds of 48 mph with a peak gust of 63 mph for 6 consecutive hours. Sustained winds of 49 mph were also reported at Cape Disappointment for 3 consecutive hours with a peak gust of 59 mph.

The Grays River near Rosburg briefly flooded March 6. The river reached flood stage around 11 am March 6th before cresting at 13.2 feet at 2 pm. The river fell below flood stage around 1 am on March 7th.
Heavy rain resulted in the Grays River near Rosburg to reach flood stage around 7 pm on March 8. The river crested at 15 feet around 1 am on March 9th and fell below flood stage around 6 pm.

Heavy rain resulted in the Nehalem River to flood near Foss. The river reached flood stage around 2 pm March 6, and crested at 14.8 feet at 8 pm. The river fell below flood stage around 9 am on March 7th.

Based on Radar and nearby reports, 6 to 12 inches of snow were followed by 0.25 to 0.5 inch of ice, leading to numerous downed trees and power outages. The Emergency Manager for Hood River County reported 8 inches of snow in Parkdale along with 0.25 inch of ice. There were several reports from the Oregon Department of Transportation of Black Ice on roads.

Based on radar and nearby reports, up to 6 inches of snow were followed by 0.5 to 1 inch of ice leading to numerous downed trees and power outages. The Eugene Water and Electric reported numerous downed power lines and shared a picture on Facebook with around an inch of ice on one of their power lines in Oakridge. This was a widespread damaging event which covered Lane County.
A trained spotter in nearby  Longview, WA reported 4 inches of snow followed by 0.1 to 0.25 inch of ice accumulation.

There were not many reports in this area, but 4 inches of snow in nearby Parkdale, OR and 9 inches in BZ Corner, OR provide an estimate of 4 to 6 inches of snow. There were also early reports of 1 to 2 inches of snow in the Gorge as the event began. There were intermittent closures on Highway 84 due to snow and icy roads.

There were not many reports in this area, but 4 inches of snow in nearby Parkdale, OR and 9 inches in BZ Corner, OR provide an estimate of 4 to 6 inches of snow. There were also early reports of 1 to 2 inches of snow in the Gorge as the event began. There were intermittent closures on Highway 84 due to snow and icy roads.
A trained spotter in Longview reported 4 inches of snow. Archived radar data estimates that this snow was over a 6 hour period.

Up to 3 inches of additional snow fell on March 8th before the precipitation changed to freezing rain in the afternoon. The freezing rain persisted through midnight. A NWS Employee reported 2.6 inches of snow followed by 0.1 inch of ice in Southwest Portland. Another NWS employee reported 2 inches of snow followed by a glaze of ice in SE Portland. A spotter in Clackamas reported 0.25 inch of ice and there were two reports in Gresham of 0.25 inch ice accumulation.

A local media meteorologist reported 0.5 to 0.75 inch of ice in Corbett. Worst impacts were near Cascade Locks where numerous crashes occurred on Interstate 84 resulting in intermittent closures due to snow and ice. There was also several power outages reported.

Although there were not many reports in the Central Columbia River Gorge, the reports that follow from the Western Columbia Gorge are near enough to verify that snow and ice also occurred in the Central Gorge. A local media meteorologist reported 0.5 to 0.75 inch of ice in Corbett. The worst impacts were near Cascade Locks where numerous crashes occurred on Interstate 84 resulting in intermittent closures due to snow and ice. There was also several power outages reported.

Up to 3 inches of additional snow fell on March 8th before the precipitation changed to freezing rain in the afternoon. The freezing rain persisted through midnight. A Battleground Spotter reported 1 inch of snow followed by 0.25 inch of ice. Another spotter reported 0.25 inch of ice accumulation in Camas.

Although there were not many reports in the Washington side of the Gorge, reports from the Oregon side can be used to verify snow and ice for the Washington side of the Columbia River Gorge. A local media meteorologist reported 0.5 to 0.75 inch of ice in Corbett, and there were numerous crashes along Interstate 84 due to snow and ice near Cascade Locks.

Although there were not many reports in the Washington side of the Gorge, reports from the Oregon side can be used to verify snow and ice for the Washington side of the Columbia River Gorge. A local media meteorologist reported 0.5 to 0.75 inch of ice in Corbett, and there were numerous crashes along Interstate 84 due to snow and ice near Cascade Locks.

The City of Portland issued its first Wireless Emergency Alert in history on March 9th at 8 AM warning people to stay indoors due to dangerous ice conditions. While most of the icing has stopped by then, there was still significant ice loading on branches and power lines as well as several of each downed. Power outages continued into the 9th due to the ice, but ice slowly melted as temperatures crept above freezing. Some ice accumulations reported from spotters include a 0.25 inch in Camas, and a 0.25 inch of ice in Battle Ground.

The City of Portland issued its first Wireless Emergency Alert in history on March 9th at 8 AM warning people to stay indoors due to dangerous ice conditions. While most of the icing has stopped by then, there was still significant ice loading on branches and power lines as well as several of each downed. Power outages continued into the 9th due to the ice, but ice slowly melted as temperatures crept above freezing. Some ice accumulations reported from spotters include a 0.30 inch in Gresham, and a 0.25 inch of ice in Clackamas. Public reports include 0.4 inch of ice in Fairview and 0.3 inch in Northeast Portland.

Heavy icing led to widespread power outages in Lane County, leaving thousands without power. A picture on the Eugene Water and Electric's Facebook page showed some downed power lines with around 1 inch of ice accumulated on them. A spotter in Lebanon reported 0.5 inch of ice and there were several reports of 0.3 to 0.75 inch ice in Eugene.

Heavy icing led to widespread power outages in Lane County, leaving thousands without power. A picture on the Eugene Water and Electric's Facebook page showed some downed power lines with around 1 inch of ice accumulated on them.

Public Utility's website reported that more than 3800 customers were without power in the Sweet Home area due to ice. Spotters reported 0.5 to 0.5 inch of ice accumulation in Salem and 0.25 inch in Dallas.
Public Utility's website reported that more than 3800 customers were without power in the Sweet Home area due to ice. A Spotter reported 0.5 inch of ice accumulation in Sweet Home.
Several SNOTEL stations reported 16 to 20 inches of snow for the Southwest Washington Cascades.

Temperatures in the single digits combined with persistent 20 to 30 mph winds produced wind chills in the -15 to -20 degrees Fahrenheit range. Timberline Lodge reported the most extreme wind chill where temperatures were as low as -5 degrees and winds gusting to 25 mph produced a wind chill as low as -31 degrees at times.
Temperatures in the single digits combined with persistent 20 to 30 mph winds produced wind chills in the -15 to -20 degrees Fahrenheit range.
Spotter reports indicated 2 to 4 inches of snow reported followed with 0.25 inch of ice.

Around 0.5 to 0.75 inch of ice accumulated in the Western Columbia River Gorge resulting in numerous reports of accidents due to icy roads on Interstate 84. A Spotter reported .25 inch in Stevenson and a local media meteorologist reported 0.75 inch in Corbett.

Around 0.5 to 0.75 inch of ice accumulated in the Western Columbia River Gorge resulting in numerous reports of accidents due to icy roads on Interstate 84. A Spotter reported .25 inch in Stevenson and a local media meteorologist reported 0.75 inch in Corbett.

There were numerous reports of snow and ice in the Central Columbia River Gorge with generally 6 to 8 inches of snow. There was a quarter of an inch of ice on top of the snow in Hood River and White Salmon.

There were numerous reports of snow and ice in the Central Columbia River Gorge with generally 6 to 8 inches of snow. There was a quarter of an inch of ice on top of the snow in Hood River and White Salmon.

There were numerous reports of snow and ice in the Central Columbia River Gorge with generally 6 to 8 inches of snow. There was a quarter of an inch of ice on top of the snow in Hood River and White Salmon, and as much as 0.4 to 0.5 inch of ice in Parkdale where the cold air held on the longest.

Significant icing closed the main road in Wind River Valley and there was a picture posted on Facebook of 0.4 to 0.5 inch of ice accumulation in this valley. This ice was after 2 to 4 inches of snow. Elsewhere in the cascades, mainly the higher elevations, received 10 to 12 inches of snow.
The Grays River near Rosburg reached flood stage around 6 am on April 24th, 2014. The river crested at 12.1 ft around 730 AM and fell below flood stage around 9 AM.

A man was struck by a large wave while rock climbing at Cape Kiwanda in Pacific City, Oregon. The wave swept him into the ocean where he drowned. His body was found May 5, 2014 near Cape Lookout in Tillamook County.
A trained spotter in nearby Longview, WA reported 4 inches of snow followed by 0.1 to 0.25 inch of ice accumulation.

Multiple sources reported that lightning struck a residence in Woodburn, OR on the Oregon Golf Association Golf Course causing a significant fire. The second floor of the home was completely destroyed.
Winds from a thunderstorm resulted in a large Oak Tree falling on two parked cars in downtown Portland.

events.cz_name: CASCADE HEAD TO FLORENCE...OUT TO 10 NM
events.event_narrative: A waterspout was observed offshore of Lincoln City, Oregon around noon on May 18th, 2014.

An injury from swimming in the Toutle River, WA during a hot weather spell could be indirectly related to the hot temperatures on July 1, 2014.  A man and two children were swimming in the Toutle River when a strong current took the three of them under water. The girl's mother jumped in to help, and also got caught in the current. The man was able to get the woman, her two daughters, and himself to shore and was later airlifted to the hospital for injuries received during the process.

A drowning in the Lewis River near Yacolt, WA is indirectly related to the hot temperatures as the victim likely went to the river to gain relief from the heat . The victim was a 44 year old man that drowned after jumping from the rocks at Moulton Falls.

A boy slipped on rocks at the Wildwood Falls near Cottage Grove, and slid around 30 feet on rocks into the water. His older brother went into the water to save the boy and both got sucked down a narrow chute of water. The younger brother survived, but the older one did not. His body was later found trapped under a large log under the chute.

Two siblings playing in the shore near Boldtad Beach was caught in a rip that dragged them out to sea. The older sibling, a 11 year old girl pushed her younger brother towards the shore before she drifted further out to sea and drowned. The younger boy was rescued after being in the water for 30 minutes. He was found with only his face above the water, and was hospitalized for injuries.

The Seaside Fire and Rescue received two seperate calls within 2 minutes of eachother to rescue a man that has been swept to sea by strong ocean currents in Seaside, OR. One man was pulled out of the ocean by 4 rescuers, and walked away with no known injuries. The other man was dragged 3 blocks south by the current, and did not survive.
