The seas were 3 feet around 11 seconds.

Heavy rain from convective showers resulted in significant flooding near Beaverton. Flooding was reported of four homes, four apartments, several garages, the Winterhawks Skating Center, and a community pool. The city Public Works Director reported 2.3 inches of rain per hour, a personal weather station reported 2.29 inches of rain over 2 hours, and the National Weather Service Doppler radar estimated 1.7 inches per hour. A car stalled in a flooded high water in an underpass near the US 26-US 217 interchange. The cost damage is an estimate based on reports from the General Manager of the Skating Center and previous history of similar residential damage.
Abundant lightning resulted in around 1000 PGE customers without power in the Albany and Corvallis area. A public caller reported that a large tree struck from lightning fell onto a home.

Media reports that a large sneaker wave took three people wading in the water near the north jetty of Tillamook out to see. Two of the people made it back to shore safely, but one did not, and was presumed to have drowned.
Heavy rain resulted in the Sandy River to rapidly rise. A foot bridge near Ramona Falls broke loose sending a man into the turbulent waters. The man drowned in the river.

The Deception Creek fire complex was started by multiple lightning storms on Aug 11, 2014.  The fire complex included the Deception Creek, Staley, Davey, Pool, Spirit and Edith fires.  The fire was approximately 7,800 burning in heavy timber.  At times, the fire came close to structures near the community of Oakridge, OR.

The Deception Creek fire complex was started by multiple lightning storms on Aug 11, 2014. The fire complex included the Deception Creek, Staley, Davey, Pool, Spirit and Edith fires. The fire was approximately 7,800 burning in heavy timber. At times, the fire came close to structures near the community of Oakridge, OR.

The Deception Creek fire complex was started by multiple lightning storms on Aug 11, 2014. The fire complex included the Deception Creek, Staley, Davey, Pool, Spirit and Edith fires. The fire was approximately 7,800 burning in heavy timber. At times, the fire came close to structures near the community of Oakridge, OR. The fire was fully contained October 24th.

The 36 Pit Wildfire resulted in evacuations of a RV park and closures of several camp grounds and recreational areas near Estacada, OR. A 5-mile stretch of Highway 224 was closed as well as some local roads and trails.

The 36 Pit Wildfire resulted in evacuations of a RV park and closures of several camp grounds and recreational areas near Estacada, OR. A 5-mile stretch of Highway 224 was closed, as well as some local roads and trails.
A member of the public noticed a cold core funnel in Newberg Oregon in the afternoon, that showed rotation for a few minutes.

A couple of people reported a cold core funnel cloud between Woodburg and Gervais, OR around 145 pm. Some damage was reported in this area around the same time, but a NWS storm survey determined the damage was more consistent with straight line wind damage than from a funnel cloud.

A convective shower resulted in minor wind damage consistent with straight line wind around 2 miles west northwest from Woodburn, OR. Several 3 to 8 inch diameter tree limbs were downed along with some smaller debris. Two 10 inch diameter rotted trees snapped and fell onto a house with no structural damage. There was also minor damage to an irrigation pipe located at the intersection of Butterville Road and LeBrun Rd. Several fences were also reported to be damaged in the area.
Wind gusts of 50 to 66 mph were reported along the North Oregon Coast with an estimated wind gust of 75 mph from a NWS Spotter near the Barview Jetty.

The Oregon Department of Transportation suggested that heavy rain was responsible for a small landslide that occurred near Corbett, Oregon. Official NWS stations reported between 0.5 to 3 inches of rain in Multnomah County in the afternoon and evening. The landslide closed both lanes of the Historic Columbia River Highway just east of the Vista House for a few hours Wednesday evening.

Law enforcement confirmed that a tornado touched down near the Safeway in Longview, WA around 1240 PM. The tornado then traveled down Vandercook Way before dissipating near Main St. There was significant roof damage to industrial buildings, minor roof damage to residential buildings, 35 to 30 large trees snapped off or blew down, some power poles downed, and automobiles damaged from debris.

The Port of Vancouver measured a peak gust of 70 mph at around the same time wind damage was reported across the Vancouver Metro Area.  One large Maple tree was snapped in Brush Prairie while another one went down near Fort Vancouver resulting in minor damage to a historical building that is now Grant's Restaurant. A person from the public reported that a 150 pound piece of a pig pen was picked up by the wind and tossed through a double-paned glass window. Clark Public Utilities reported 4,500 homes experienced electricity outages.
The Abernathy RAWS reported a maximum wind gust of 57 mph between 6 and 7 pm PST.
The Coast Guard reported a peak gust of 75 mph at Ilwaco at 345 PM PST. Close to that time, Toke Point reported a peak gust of 65 mph, and Cape Disappointment had a peak gust of 60 mph.
The Three Corner Rock RAWS reported a sustained wind of 60 mph with a peak gust of 81 mph.

Several locations reported very strong winds with gusts greater than 55 mph along the North Oregon Coast with the most noteworthy, a 87 mph gust measured at Cape Meares. A NWS spotter in Tillamook, Oregon had a rain gutter displaced from the roof as well as bolts ripped out of an automatic push door.

Several stations along the Central Oregon coast reported sustained winds greater than 48 mph with gusts greater than 60 mph. The strongest peak gust of 85 mph was measured at the Sea Lions Cave, with the second highest being 76 mph on the Yaquina Bridge.
The Oregon Department of Transportation reported all lanes on Highway 18 as a large tree blocked the lanes. Shortly after, Mount Hebo reported a 78 mph gust.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Oregon Department of Transportation closed both lanes of Highway 18 since a large downed tree was blocking the lanes. The Rock House RAWS measured sustained winds of 40 mph with a peak gust of 62 mph, and the BPA station at Marys Peak recorded a peak gust of 91 mph.

Wind gusts up to 60 mph were reported throughout the Portland Metro Area. There were numerous trees downed by these winds with some landing on power lines. There was at least two homes that had major damage due to downed trees. Portland General Electric reported around 140,000 people without power by the end of the storm. One downed power line burned a hole in the road that it fell on. A NWS employee reported that a large gust blew doors open at a SW Portland restaurant, and ripped large paintings off the wall. Some of the downed trees blocked roads, and 2 lanes were blocked on Highway 30 for a couple of hours.
Portland General Electric reported thousands of power outages from Winds and Trees downing power lines.

Strong wind gusts resulted in several large trees downed in the South Willamette Valley. One tree damaged a car port. Several power lines were downed by the winds causing widespread power outages and sometimes blocking roads. Highway 99 was closed between Highway 36 and 1st Street in junction City due to a downed power line.
High winds resulted in several downed tree branches and power lines, resulting in widespread power outages.

A couple of reports from the Public described a funnel cloud around 10 miles north of Brownsville, Oregon. One of the reports came from an off-duty police dispatcher that confirmed rotation with the cloud.

The Oregon Department of Transportation reported land and mud slides near Estacada, Oregon after 2 inches of rain fell over the past week. These slides closed Higway 226 near milepost 36 for several of days.
Thunderstorms produced a downburst of wind that downed around 50 Douglas Fir trees with trunk diameters between 10 and 14 inches.
A Pacific County Sheriff officer took photos of very large hail that fell near the Naselle-Grays River School District Office. The size of the hail was estimated to have a 1.25 inch diameter.
Frost on the roads and bridges resulted in several traffic accidents, including one fatality on Highway 103 near the US-26 intersection.

The Grays River near Rosburg reached the flood stage of 12 feet at 715 AM PST on December 20th. The river crested at 13.6 feet at 12:15 AM PST on December 21 before falling below flood stage at 8:15 AM PST.

The Siletz River at Siletz reached flood stage of 20 feet at 1045 PM PST on December 20th. The river crested at 20.33 feet at 1230 AM PST on December 21st, before dropping below flood stage an hour later.

The Siuslaw River near Mapelton reached the flood stage of 22 feet at 1115 PM PST on December 20th. The river crested at 22.8 feet at 330 AM PST on December 21st, and dropped below flood stage at noon on the 21st.

The Alsea River near Tidewater reached flood stage of 18 feet at 1030 pm PST on December 20th. The river crested at 18.89 feet at 230 AM PST on December 21st, and dropped below flood stage at 1130 AM PST.
The Wilson River near Tillamook reached flood stage of 12 feet at 630 PM on December 20th. The river crested at 14.12 feet at 830 AM on December 21st, and dropped below flood stage at 1045 AM.

The Clackamas River near Estacada reached flood stage of 20 feet at 830 AM PST on December 21st. The river crested at 20.27 feet at 1030 AM on December 21st, before dropping below flood stage at 2 pm.
The Luckiamute river near Suver reached flood stage of 27 feet around 820 AM PST on December 21st. The river crested at 30.46 feet at 3 PM, and dropped below flood stage later that evening.

The Mary's River near Philomath reached flood stage of 20 feet at 830 AM PST on December 21st. The river crested at 20.45 feet, just 0.5 feet below the major flood category around 530 AM PST on December 22nd.
The Oregon Department of Transportation reported that heavy rain resulted in a rockslide that blocked Highway 99E in Oregon City.
The RAWS station at Larch Mountain measured a peak gust of 67 mph.

Winds in the Vancouver metro area gusted 45 to 60 mph for around 10 hours. Several trees and power lines were downed by high winds near Arnada Park, three homes were damaged by downed trees in Camas, and a 18 to 20 inch diameter tree snapped near the base in Battleground. A NWS employee in the eastern suburbs of Vancouver recorded a 55 mph wind gust.

Strong winds resulted in downed trees throughout the metro area. Downed trees were responsible for the shut down of several sections of the MAX line for several hours, and the closures of Cornelius Pass Road and Shattuck Road. One tree crashed the roof of a house in Oregon City and pinned the resident under a desk inside. A biker sustained serious injuries when a tree fell on him and a near by car. A 54 mph easterly wind gust at the Portland Airport was the strongest east wind recorded since 1989.
The Abernathy RAWS measured sustained winds of 38 mph with a peak gust of 58 mph.
Two weather stations on the North Oregon Coast measured wind gusts of 63 mph, one at Garibaldhi and the other in Pacific City.

Six weather stations on the Central Oregon Coast measured wind gusts greater than 58 mph for at least 2 hours. The highest gust of 82 mph was recorded at Sea Lions Caves. The next highest gust, 70 mph, was measured in Newport at the Yaquina Bar.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: Mary's Peak recorded a peak gust of 90 mph, and the Rockhouse RAWS measured a peak gust of 62 mph.
There were numerous reports of 5 to 8 inches of snow in 12 hours in the Upper Hood River Valley.
There were numerous reports of 5 to 8 inches of snow in 12 hours for the Central Columbia River Gorge.

A combination of heavy snow and ice resulted in slick driving conditions for the Western Columbia River Gorge. Areas in the gorge measured a quarter of an inch of ice whereas other areas had 5 to 8 inches of snow.
Several stations reported 10 to 12 inches of snow for the Cascades with some reporting rates greater than an inch per hour.
Spotters reported around 6 to 8 inches of snow for the Cascade Foothills followed by a quarter of an inch of ice.
There were numerous reports of 5 to 8 inches of snow for the Central Columbia River Gorge.
There were several reports of 5 to 8 inches of snow in the Western Columbia River Gorge in less than 12 hours. This snow was followed with a quarter of an inch of ice in many locations.

The Central Willamette Valley had a quarter to a half of inch of ice. Numerous trees and large limbs were downed and or snapped by the weight of the ice. One tree crashed and injured a teen standing on a sidewalk in Salem.
There were several reports of a quarter to a halfo of an inch of accumulated ice in the Southern Willamette Valley. Numerous trees and large limbs were downed or snapped by the weight of the ice.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Central Oregon Coast Range were especially hit hard with ice, with many areas reporting a half of inch of ice. An Emergency Manger that was visiting the area said that there were local spots with close to 2 inches of ice. A spotter in Blodgett, who has spent there entire life there, reported that this was the worst ice storm that they had ever seen. Numerous trees and large branches fell or snapped due to the weight of the ice.

Most areas measured a tenth of an inch of ice in the Portland metro Area, but there were local areas, near Gresham and Troutdale where there was a quarter of an inch of ice. This ice resulted in transportation impacts for the Gresham area including the closure of Stark Street and Corbett Hill Road.
Clatsop Spit measured 43 mph sustained winds with peak gusts to 51 mph.
Grays River near Rosburg reached flood stage of 12 feet at 1205 AM on January 5th, and crested around 15.4 feet at 815 AM. The river fell below flood stage around 1030 PM.

The Naselle River near Naselle reached flood stage of 15.5 feet at 410 AM on January 5th. The river crested at the major flood stage of 17 feet around 745 AM before dropping below flood stage at 1150 AM.

The Washington Department of Transportation reported Westbound State Route 4 was closed at mile post 21 due to a rock or mud slide resulting from heavy rain. The rain gauge at nearby KM Mountain measured 2 inches of rain in the 6 hour period leading up to the slide.
Sustained winds of 44 mph with a peak gust of 56 mph was reported at Clatsop Spit between 8 pm on December 8th through 945 AM on December 9th.
Two weather stations at or near Garibaldi reported measured wind gusts at or near 70 mph on December 9th with sustained winds around 50 mph. These winds were observed for 6 to 8 hours.

Two stations near the beaches of the Southwest Washington Coast, Cape Disappointment and Toke Point measured sustained winds between 40 and 45 mph from the afternoon of December 8th through the morning of December 9th. Cape Disappointment also measured a peak gust of 56 mph.

Two weather stations, Garibaldi and Clatsop Spit, reported sustained wind speeds around 42 mph on December 10th with a peak wind gust of 70 mph measured at Garibaldi. The Oregon Department of Transportation reported that the winds knocked a tree over onto power lines on US Highway 26 near milepost 3 resulting in a partial closure of the highway.
Several weather stations reported wind gusts greater than 62 mph on December 10th with the highest wind gust of 72 mph reported at Yaquina Bridge.
The Oregon Department of Transportation reported that strong winds downed a tree onto power lines on US Highway 26 near milepost 3. This downed tree resulted in a partial closure of the highway.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Bonneville Power Administration weather station at Mary's Peak measured sustained winds around 50 mph with frequent gusts to 75 mph for several hours on December 10th. The peak gust at this station was measured at 93 mph.
Cape Disappointment and Toke Point reported sustained winds around 46 mph on December 10th with the highest measured gust of 62 mph at Toke Point.
Four weather stations along the North Oregon coast reported sustained winds between 37 and 51 mph in the afternoon on December 11th. The highest wind gust was 63 mph  reported at Garibaldi.

Ten weather stations measured sustained winds greater than 38 mph with gusts greater than 58 mph. The highest gust of 9 mph was from the Sea Lion Caves with the second highest of 76 mph reported from a National Weather Service Spotter located in Newport. Numerous power outages were reported.
A HAM Radio operator reported that Mount Hebo measured a peak gust of 90 mph. Another weather station near Forest Grove reported a gust of 58 mph.

Gusty strong winds resulted in several downed trees for the Portland Metro Area. There were widespread road closures and power outages due to the downed trees. One fatality and one injury resulted from a tree falling onto a moving car. The Portland International Airport experienced re routing and delays of aircraft, and the Portland Mass Transit, MAX system had system-wide delays due to power outages. In downtown Portland, loose material from a roof of a nearby building were lofted and blown against windows of the Standard Insurance Plaza damaging several windows on the fifteenth floor. A Parapet of a Portland apartment in NW Portland fell and caused major damage to the apartment building. At least one power pole was downed by the winds in Washington County. A large tree fell onto a moving car injuring a mother and killing her son.

Strong winds resulted in several downed trees and power outages. One tree damaged the roof of a home in Dayton.  Peak wind gusts for the Aurora and McMinnville Airports measured at 61 mph, and wind a peak wind gust of 71 mph was measured at Chehalem Mountain.

Sustained winds of 40 mph were reported at the Eugene Airport, but there were reports of at least 3 large trees downed. One of these trees fell on top of a SUV in Albany. The strong winds also resulted in numerous power outages in the Corvallis area.
Two Weather Stations along the Southwest Washington Coast measured wind gusts around 63 mph for a couple of hours in the evening.

Two Weather observers reported measured wind gusts around 58 mph in Vancouver and a peak gust of 60 mph was reported on the Glen Jackson Bridge on Interstate 205. These strong winds resulted in numerous downed trees and tree limbs in the Vancouver metro area, and widespread power outages.
Three weather stations along the Central Oregon Coast reported strong gusty winds in excess of 56 mph. The strongest gust was 62 mph measured at the Yaquina Bridge in Newport.

A weather station near the Timberline Lodge measured a wind gust of 121 mph with sustained winds of 92 mph. This station reported nine consecutive hours of wind greater than 100 mph. Santiam pass which usually is conservative on wind reports recorded a peak wind gust of 67 mph. The chair lifts at Mount Hood Meadows were closed due to the strong winds.
A peak gust of 61 mph was measured at Abernathy Mountain. Strong gusty winds persisted at this location for eight consecutive hours.
A peak wind gust of 77 mph was measured at the Three Corner Rock Weather station.

Various of stations reported 0.25 to 0.4 inch of ice accumulation including Parkdale and Middle Mountain. A newspaper article reported a fatal car crash due to ice on Highway 26 in Wasco County, just northeast of the upper hood river valley.
Various weather stations reported conditions favorable for accumulating ice in the valleys of the Southwest Washington Cascades, and it is estimated that there was 0.25 to 0.4 inch of ice.
Wind and temperatures measurements for Mount Hood Meadows resulted in a wind chill of negative 26 degrees Celsius.

East winds blowing through the gorge were strong enough to knock over trees in the Portland Metro area resulting in minor damage. One tree in Southwest Portland came down onto a house. Another tree knocked down near the Sellwood Bridge resulted in the closing of Highway 43 and caused major traffic delays. Several trees were knocked down in Gresham with at least one falling down on power lines and causing power outages. Another tree in Gresham fell onto a car.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Rockhouse RAWS measured a maximum gust of 63 mph in the early evening. A national Weather Service Spotter also reported shingle damage to their roof and observed small tree limbs downed by the wind.
A Department of Transportation sensor measure sustained winds of 40 mph.
A Department of Transportation sensor measured sustained winds of 40 mph on Sauvie Island.

Sustained winds at Garibaldi, Tillamook, and Pacific City measured 40 to 48 mph with gusts 58 to 60 mph. A National Weather Spotter in Tillamook witnessed these winds toss a large trampoline into a nearby tree.
Several weather stations on the Central Oregon Coast reported gusty winds with the strongest gust of 65 mph measured in Yachats and Gleneden Beach.
The weather station at Mount Hebo measured sustained winds of 49 mph with a peak gust of 81 mph, and sustained winds of 39 mph with a peak gust of 61 mph was measured at Tidewater.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: A peak gust of 99 mph was measured at Mary's Peak with sustained winds of 57 mph. The Rockhouse RAWS station recorded a peak gust of 65 mph.
A weather station at Timberline recorded gusty winds for around 8 hours. The sustained winds were around 70 mph and a peak gust of 111 mph was measured. The winds periodically gusted above 100 mph.
Sustained winds around 44 mph were measured for an hour at Cape Disappointment.
The Abernathy RAWS measured a peak gust of 64 mph.
The Three Corner RAWS measured sustained winds around 52 mpg with a peak gust of 82 mph.

A sneaker wave surprised some children who jumped on a log to avoid getting wet. The wave lifted the log which then rolled onto a 10 year old boy. The boy was seriously injured including bone fractures, collapsed lungs and a lacerated liver.

Sustained winds around 48 mph were measured for three hours along the North Oregon Coast with gusts around 62 mph reported at Garibaldi and on the Megler Bridge. A National Weather Spotter reported a wind gust of 57 mph in Pacific City.
Sustained winds of 47 mph and a peak gust of 62 mph was reported on the Megler Bridge.
Sustained winds around 48 mph were measured along the North Oregon Coast. A gust up to 65 mph was measured at Megler Bridge.
A cold front brought a burst of strong winds to the South Washington Coast.
Sustained winds of 47 mph was observed at Megler Bridge with gusts to 64 mph.
Sustained winds of 47 mph was observed at Megler Bridge with a peak gust of 64 mph.
Sustained winds of 45 mph was observed at Yaquina Bridge with a peak gust of 61 mph.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: A peak wind gust of 60 mph was measured at the Rockhouse RAWS station, and a peak gust of 80 mph was measured at the higher elevation of Marys Peak.

Several weather stations along the Central Oregon Coast reported gusty winds. Sustained winds were generally around 40 mph with gusts around 60 mph. However, Florence reported a peak gust of 79 mph, and Yachats had a gust of 72 mph.
The Grays River reached the flood stage of 12 feet at 935 AM on February 6th. The river crested at 13.9 feet at 218 PM, and dropped below flood stage at 850 PM.
A mudslide crossed Northwest Marlborough Street into a residential garage after 3 to 6 inches of rain fell across Northwest Oregon.

Around 50 trees were downed by strong winds in the afternoon on March 15 in the Portland Metro area. A large tree fell onto a jeep and trapped a injured driver for several hours. Scaffolding was knocked off of a building downtown onto a few cars. A large tree even fell in the parking lot of the National Weather Service Forecast Office. Siding of a chimney in Southwest Portland was peeled off by the winds. Several roads were closed from trees and there were bus and train delays due to power outages. Four airplanes on route to Portland were diverted to other cities. A peak gust of 70 mph was measured at Chehalem Mountain, and a BPA weather station in Troutdale measured gusts of 63 mph.
A spotter in Canby measured a wind gust of 60 mph, and the Salem Airport measured a gust of 58 mph. Several trees were downed in the area with one large tree falling and damaging a house in Yamhill.

A trained spotter measured a wind gust of 70 mph at the Barview Jetty. There were several weather stations along the coast that measured sustained winds greater than 40 mph and gusts greater than 59 mph. The strongest gust of 83 mph was measured at Garibaldi. The second strongest wind gust was 74 mph measured in Lincoln City.

Several stations along the Central Oregon Coast measured sustained winds greater than 45 mph and gusts greater than 60 mph. The ASOS at the Newport Airport measured a wind gust of 68 mph. The strongest wind gust of 71 mph was measured on the Yaquina Bridge.
The Columbia River Fire and Rescue confirmed that a few large trees fell onto the Gable Park Apartment Building resulting in the displacement of 15 people. The trees also damaged a few cars.

A Spotter in Battleground reported a measured wind gust of 58 mph. An Oregon Department of Transportation weather station on the interstate bridge measured a peak gust of 57 mph for a couple of hours.

A spotter reported two large trees downed by strong winds in Ocean Park. One of the trees fell onto and broke a power line. Sustained winds of 57 mph were measured at Cape Disappointment with a peak gust of 75 mph. Wind gusts around 60 mph were measured at Toke Point and Megler Bridge.
A Funnel cloud was reported over Evergreen Estates near the corner of 11th Street and Evergreen Court.
A funnel cloud was reported near the Blimp Hanger at the Tillamook Airport. The report was relayed by the Tillamook County Emergency Manager and was accompanied by  photos.

A Lane Community College Official witnessed a rain wrapped tornado that significantly damaged three vehicles. One vehicle was moved around 125 feet and ended upside down on a berm in a parking lot. Estimated wind speeds of 65 to 85 mph is needed to move a car which rates the tornado as an EF0.
The RAWS station at Abernathy measured a peak gust of 62 mph.
High Winds were measured near and around the coast range on Northwest Oregon. Chehalem Mountain measured a peak gust of 70 mph.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Rockhouse RAWS measured sustained winds of 45 mph with gusts to 65 mph for five hours. A peak gust of 86 mph was measured at Marys Peak.

A Tualtain news reporter witnessed sudden heavy rain cause standing water on roadways shortly before a member of the public reported flooding on the roads between Sherwood and Tualatin. The water on the roads was reported to be as high as a car's wheel well. The Washington County Scanner then reported manholes being removed due to flowing water on roadways due to heavy rain. A rain gauge in the nearby Yamhill County measured 1.75 inches in 2 hours with 0.91 inches measured between 613 and 628 pm.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms was reported in Hillsboro, Banks, Forest Grove, Gaston, Cornelius, and Aloha. A member of the public reported on Facebook that 0.84 inches of rain fell in 30 minutes near Banks. There were several reports of ponding on highway 6 and highway 8 that resulted in the hydroplaning of many cars. There was a Twitter report that Baseline Rd had around an inch of standing water. A blogger reported that the heavy rain could not keep up with the storm drains, and flooded a neighbors house.
A member of the public supplied a video and photo of a funnel cloud to a local news station.
A member of the public reported a funnel in Aumsville around 8 pm.

High Temperatures were in the low 90s June 7 through June 9th which is around 20 degrees higher than the seasonal normals. There is one known indirect heat related fatality where a teenager boy drowned while swimming in the Lewis River near Woodland. Newspaper articles suggest that he may have suffered from hypothermia paralysis from the cold water.

High Temperatures were in the low to mid 90s June 7 through June 9th which is around 22 degrees higher than the seasonal normals. The low temperatures were also unseasonably warm and the low temperature on June 7 of 61 degrees at the Portland Airport tied the warmest low record that was previously set in 1948.  There is one known indirect heat related fatality where a young man boy drowned while swimming in the Clackamas River near Gladstone. Multnomah County had 7 hospital visits for heat related illnesses.

Maximum temperatures were in the mid to upper 90s which is 20 to 25 degrees above the seasonal normals. The low temperatures were in the mid 60s to low 70s. Several new daily temperature records were set for the warmest low temperatures. One man drowned after he fell off a jet ski in the Columbia River on June 27th. This accident occurred around 1 AM, but the warm nighttime temperatures likely contributed to him going into the river at night. The Multnomah County had 10 emergency room visits for heat related illnesses.

Afternoon temperatures were in the low to mid 90s which is around 20 degrees above normal. Nighttime temperatures were in the mid 60s to low 70s which is around 15 degrees above normal. There were several new daily records set for the warmest low temperatures. A man drowned while swimming in the Santiam River on June 28th.

Afternoon temperatures were in the low to mid 90s which is around 20 degrees higher than the seasonal normals. The low temperatures were in the mid to upper 60s which is around 10 degrees above the seasonal normal. Several new daily temperature records were set for the warmest low temperatures. A man drowned while swimming in the Lewis River on June 27th.

High Temperatures were in the mid to upper 90s July 1 through July 5th which is around 15 degrees higher than the seasonal normal. The low temperatures were also unseasonably warm. The low temperature on July 2 of 67 degrees at the Portland Airport broke the previous warmest low record of 63 degrees last set in 2013. There is one known indirect heat related injury where a young boy was rescued from Oregon Lake in Fairview, Oregon.

High Temperatures were in the upper 90s to low 100s July 1 through July 5th in the South Willamette Valley which is around 15 degrees higher than the seasonal normal. The daily high temperature at Eugene broke the previous daily high temperature records for three consecutive days. There is one known indirect fatality where a man drowned while floating down the Willamette River near Bowman Park in Albany.

High Temperatures were in the upper 90s to around 105 for the Southern Willamette Valley. The daily maximum temperature of 105 degrees at Eugene broke the previous record of 99 last set in 2003. Local newspapers reported 3 separate incidents where children were left in hot cars in the Eugene area.
A man swimming along the coast near Tillamook was unable to swim to shore because of a rip current, and drowned.

A teen was wading in the ocean when he was swept out to see, and was unable to make it back to shore. His friend tried to save him, and also got swept out to sea, but  was able to make it back to shore. The teen struggled for more than 10 minutes in the water before a local fire crew rescued him and took him to the hospital.
High Temperatures were in the mid 90s to near 100, July 1 through July 5th which is around 15 degrees higher than the seasonal normal. The low temperatures were also unseasonably warm.

High Temperatures were in the upper 90s to around 103 for the northern Willamette Valley. Emergency Preparedness officials opened cooling shelters.  Several people were treated for heat related illnesses at medical centers.

High Temperatures were in the upper 90s to around 105 for the central Willamette Valley. Emergency Preparedness officials opened cooling shelters. A few people were treated for heat related illnesses at medical centers.

High Temperatures were in the upper 90s to around 103 for Clark County and greater Vancouver area. Emergency Preparedness officials opened cooling shelters. A few people were treated for heat related illnesses at medical centers.

Temperatures peaked in the mid to upper 90s which is 10 to 15 degrees above the seasonal normal. The daily high temperature on the 18th of 98 degrees at the Hillsboro airport tied the previous record last set in 1996. The high temperature of 96 degrees on the 19th at the Portland International Airport broke the previous records of 93 last set in 1946. The temperature at the Portland airport on the 19th of 97 degrees tied the previous record last set in 1967. The Troutdale Airport also broke a new temperature record on the 18th of 97 degrees where the previous record was 94 last set in 1967.

Wind Gusts above 58 mph were reported for several stations along the North Coast with the highest measured gust of 90 mph at Oceanside. There were several reports of downed trees and power lines across Tillamook County. Tents and booths at the Hood to Coast Relay finish line in Seaside were damaged by Strong winds.
Several stations reported peak gusts greater than 58 mph along the Central Oregon Coast with the highest gust of 63 mph measured at Yachats.
The winds at Mount Hebo measured above 58 mph with a peak gust of 60 mph. A near by station measured just under 58 mph. Near by Marys Peak measured a peak gust of 86 mph.

Several locations measured wind gusts greater than 35 mph with the highest wind of 50 mph measured near the Oregon Zoo. There were several reports of downed trees and power lines that resulted in the loss of power for around 28,000 residents. Downed power lines closed Marine Drive, and a downed tree blocked a lane on US 30 on the Interstate 405 ramp at Therman. A twitter report showed a photo of downed tree damage to a couple of parked cars.
A Funnel Cloud was spotted by a driver driving on I-5 around noon.
The NWS received several reports of a funnel cloud near Hillsboro in the afternoon, including one report from a county official.

Heavy rain resulted in Flooding of the Grays River. Grays River reached flood stage at 1230 pm on October 31, and crested at 14.7 feet at 415 pm. The river dropped below flood stage at 1215 AM November 1st. The local Sheriff confirmed that water from the river flooded the nearby Covered Bridge Road.

There were several reports of 3 to 4 inches of 24-hour Rain totals in Clark County. A trained spotter reported that the Washougal River was near bank full. Another weather spotter reported a minor mudslide on Washougal River Road between mile posts 3 and 4 where the debris was 3 inches deep. An Emergency Manager claimed were three residential floodings, several places with high water, and two road closures (Southeast Mill Plain and Southeast Village Loop).

Heavy rain combined with clogged drains from leaves resulted in urban flooding. The Portland Fire and Rescue received 32 calls in regards to street flooding, and assisted travelers in 5 cars from their stalled or trapped cars to dry land. Four roads were closed in the area for high water, and several Max lines were cancelled due to flooding under bridges. Thirteen Max trains were damaged by water and will be out of service for up to 2 weeks. One roof collapsed from the weight of rain water after the roof drains had been clogged, and several homes or businesses had flooded basements. A tree had fallen onto and damaged a parked car.

Heavy rain combined with clogged drains resulted in small stream and urban flooding. There were 16 instances where water or agricultural debris needed to be cleared from roadways. At least two residential basements were flooded in Beaverton. A large basement of an office building was flooded in Hillsboro.
A fisherman observed a water spout over the columbia river near buoy 10, and submitted a photo of it to the local station KATU.
There were several reports of a funnel cloud in the vicinity of Coburg, OR.
The Abernathy RAWS station reported a peak gust of 68 mph, and a peak gust of 73 mph was reported at the Naselle Bridge.

The Oregon Department of Transportation weather station on Megler Bridge reported a maximum gust of 63 mph. Another weather station reported sustained winds of 44 mph with a peak gust of 53 mph at Cape Disappointment.
A peak gust of 55 mph was reported at the Astoria Airport, and sustained winds of 48 mph with gusts to 56 mph were measured at Garibaldi. The highest gust of 63 mph was measured on the Megler Bridge.

The RAWS station at Tidewater measured sustained winds of 22 mph with gusts to 35 mph for several hours with a peak gust of 50 mph. Shortly after the 50 mph gust, 2 trees were downed in Vernonia. One of the trees fell onto a power line.

A weather station on the Naselle Bridge measured sustained winds of 48 mph with a peak gust of 72 mph. Strong winds were also reported at the Abernathy RAWS station where a peak gust of 67 mph was measured.
Sustained winds of 43 mph with a peak gust of 53 mph was measured at a Cape Disappointment weather station. Maximum sustained winds of 45 mph was also reported at Megler Bridge.
The Oregon Department of Transportation's weather station at Megler Bridge reported sustained winds of 45 mph.
A weather station at Gleneden Beach measured a peak gust of 63 mph.
A weather station at Mount Hebo measured sustained winds of 45 mph with a peak gust of 69 mph. A different station at Mount Hebo reported a peak gust of 61 mph.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Rockhouse RAWS measured sustained winds of 40 mph with a peak gust of 61 mph.

The 5 day rainfall total ending in the morning on November 17th for Lees Camp, OR was 14.60 inches. Flooding from this rain closed several roads including Highway 101, Highway 6, Long Prairie Road, Alderbrook Road, God's Valley Road, and Front Street. Emergency response officials evacuated residents and about 20 trailers at two trailer parks (one near the Wilson River and one near the Tilamook River). Two of the trailers were damaged by the flooding. Flooding of Lake Lytle in Rockaway Beach flooded an apartment. The Wilson River near Tillamook, the Nehalem River near Foss, and the Trask River near Tillamook all exceeded flood stage with the Wilson cresting at 17.71 feet, the Nehalem at 17.71 feet, and the Trask at 18.56 feet. Flooding of the Trask River flooded a garage. Heavy rain also produced 2 minor mud slides.

Several roads were closed due to water on the roadways including Covered Bridge Road, Eden Valley Road, Satterland Road, Foster Road, and West End Loop Road. Grays River near Rosburg exceeded flood stage early in the morning on the 17th then exceeded major flood stage in the evening. The river crested at 16.09 feet, and fell below flood stage around 2 pm Wednesday afternoon. Heavy rain also resulted in a small landslide near milepost 2 on Altoona Pillar Rock Road.

Five day rainfall totals ending in the morning of Nov 17th in the Willapa Hills were 8 to 12 inches. This rain resulted in the Willapa River to exceed flood stage around 11 pm on the 17th. The River crested at 21.12 feet which is 1.1 feet above flood stage.
Heavy rain caused the Cowlitz River near Kelso to flood. The river crested at 22.1 feet, which is 0.6 ft above flood stage.
The weather station at Cape Disappointment measured sustained winds of 56 mph with a maximum gust of 63 mph.

A weather station at Naselle Ridge reported sustained winds of 58 mph with a peak gust of 86 mph. Gusts up to 90 mph was measured by the Abernathy RAWS. The Wahkiakum County Emergency Manager reported 8 to 10 trees were downed by the wind and blocked several roads across the area.
The Three Corner Rock RAWS measured sustained winds of 60 mph with a peak gust of 90 mph. Another weather station near Augspurger measured a gust of 80 mph.
Strong west winds downed several trees along Highway 14.
The weather station at the Bonneville Dam measured a peak gust of 69 mph. Strong west winds downed several trees along Highway 14.
Several weather stations measured sustained winds around 40 mph with gusts in the 50+ mph range. THe BPA weather station in Tillamook measured a peak gust of 63 mph.
The Tidewater RAWS station measured sustained winds of 47 mph with a peak gust of 72 mph. A wind gust of 86 mph was measured at Mount Hebo.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Rockhouse RAWS measured a peak gust of 63 mph, and the near by BPA weather station at Mary's Peak measured a peak gust of 76mph.
The Middle Mountain RAWS measured a peak gust of 63 mph, and a rare west wind gust of 55 mph was measured in Parkdale.
Strong winds downed 24 trees along Interstate 84, and closed the freeway overnight.
Strong west winds downed 24 trees along Interstate 84 and closed the highway overnight.
A funnel Cloud was observed near the Evergreen Vineyards in McMinnville.

A 80 year old woman was trapped in bed all night after strong winds uprooted a large fir tree that fell on her house. The tree split the house in half.  Several days of heavy rain contributed to weakened root system from saturated soils.
A weather station in Florence, OR measured 40 mph sustained winds.
Sustained winds of 46 mph was measured at Cape Disappointment late in the morning through early in the afternoon with a peak gust of 56 mph.
Sustained winds of 41 mph were measured at Cape Disappointment for several hours with a peak gust of 51 mph.
The Abernathy RAWS station measured sustained winds of 43 mph for several hours and a peak gust of 62 mph.

Weather stations at Cape Disappointment and on the Megler Bridge measured sustained winds of 56 mph with a peak gust of 67 mph measured at Cape Disappointment. A peak gust of 62 mph was also measured at Toke Point.
The Abernathy RAWS measured sustained winds of 48 mph with a peak gust of 72 mph.

Several weather stations along the North Oregon Coast measured high winds. Sustained winds ranged from 36 to 56 mph and the highest gust recorded was 60 mph in Pacific City. The Tillamook County Emergency Manager reported that 4200 residents in the county were without power due to the winds.
Several weather stations along the Central Oregon Coast measured high winds. Sustained winds ranged from 36 mph to 52 mph and the highest wind gust of 68 mph was measured in Florence.
The Tidewater RAWS measured sustained winds of 42 mph with a peak gust of 69 mph, and nearby Mt. Hebo measured a peak gust of 85 mph.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Rockhouse RAWS measured high winds for a few hours with a peak gust of 79 mph. A peak gust of 92 mph was measured at Mary's Peak.
The Oregon Department of Highway's weather station on Megler Bridge measured sustained winds of 56 mph.
The Abernathy RAWS measured sustained winds of 48 mph for several hours and a peak gust of 83 mph.
The Three Corner Rock RAWS measured sustained winds of 56 mph for a few hours, and a peak gust of 86 mph.

The media reported that strong winds resulted in tree damage near 5th and Jefferson in Oregon City. There was another report of a 1.5 diameter evergreen tree that fell onto a home in Clackamas and damaged the roof.
The media reported that several downed trees closed Highway 26 in Rhododendron.
Several weather stations along the South Washington Coast measured sustained winds between 40 and 45 mph for many hours, and a peak gust of 54 mph was measured at Cape Disappointment.
The Abernathy RAWS measured a peak gust of 75 mph.

The Three Corner Rock RAWS measured two surges of strong winds on December 8th, once between 11 am and 2 pm, and then again between 5 pm and 9 pm. The sustained winds during these two time periods was 56 mph. A peak gust of 77 mph was reported in the first surge, and a peak gust of 92 mph was measured in the evening.

Several weather stations along the North Oregon Coast reported high winds with sustained winds ranging between 41 and 51 mph. The strongest wind gust was 88 mph at Cape Meares. The Clatsop and Tillamook County Emergency Managers reported several trees downed from the winds with widespread power outages. A tree fell onto at least one home in Tillamook.

Several stations along the Central Oregon Coast measured high winds with sustained winds ranging between 40 and 49 mph. The highest wind gust recorded was 60 mph in Lincoln City. An official NWS Spotter reported that the winds were snapping large tree branches that were littering the roadways.

Several weather stations in the Northwest Oregon coast range reported high winds with sustained winds between 34 and 40 mph. The highest gust recorded was 91 mph at the Mount Hebo Tower. The BPA station at Mount Hebo also measured a peak gust of 68 mph.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: A couple of stations measured high winds in the Central Oregon Coast Range with sustained winds between 40 and 60 mph. A peak wind gust of 97 mph was measured at Marys Peak. The Rockhouse RAWS measured a peak gust of 69 mph. An official NWS Spotter in Blodgett reported that several branches were down and the shingles on the home were flapping in the wind.

Strong winds combined with saturated soils from heavy rainfall resulted in property damage around the Portland metro area. A tree fell down and resulted in extensive damage to a home in Aloha. Another tree fell onto a home in Portland, killing a woman. Winds also damaged the Milwaukie Bridge.  Broken tree limbs fell onto power lines that resulted in widespread power outages in Portland, Clackamas, and Beaverton.

A county official reported that a tree blew onto a home in Mulino near Union Mils Road. A roof was also blown off of an old tool shed. There was also reports of several downed trees in the area with some blocking roads.  Soils were extremely saturated from heavy rainfall.
Several weather stations along the South Washington coast measured high winds with the highest wind gust of 67 mph reported at Cape Disappointment.
The Three Corner Raws measured sustained wind of 54 mph with a peak gust of 81 mph.
Several weather stations along the North Oregon Coast measured high winds with sustained winds ranging between 40 and 45 mph. The highest recorded wind gust was  63 mph on the Megler Bridge.
Many of the weather stations along the Central Oregon Coast measured high winds with sustained winds between 40 and 49 mph. The highest recorded wind gust was 79 mph at Gleneden Beach.
A couple of weather stations across the Northwest Oregon Coast Range measured high winds with wind gusts between 59 and 67 mph.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Rockhouse RAWS measured a peak gust of 81 mph.
Wind damage from thunderstorm winds were reported in Eugene and Creswell. Numerous trees were downed on vehicles and buildings, and downed power lines resulted in widespread electricity outages.
The media reported that a home in Aloha sustained significant damage as a tree downed by strong winds fell onto it.
A weather station at Cape Disappointment measured sustained winds of 51 mph with a peak gust of 65 mph.
The Abernathy RAWS measured sustained winds of 47 mph with a peak gust of 78 mph.
Several stations along the North Oregon Coast measured high winds with sustained winds between 37 and 43 mph. THe highest recorded wind gust was 61 mph at Pacific City.
Several stations along the Central Oregon Coast measured high winds with sustained winds between 41 and 47 mph. A peak gust was recorded of 60 mph at Yachats.

A few weather stations along the North Oregon coast measured high winds with sustained winds between 47 and 51 mph. The highest recorded gust of 92 mph was measured at Cape Meares and 74 mph at Garabaldi.

Several stations along the Central Oregon Coast measured high winds with sustained winds between 40 and 50 mph. The highest recorded wind gust was 77 mph at the Newport Jetty and 72 mph on the Yaquina Bridge in Newport.
A couple of weather stations along the Central Oregon Coast measured peak wind gusts of 60 to 61 mph.
A weather station at Cape Disappointment measured sustained winds of 40 mph with a peak gust of 62 mph.
Sustained winds of 47 mph was measured at Megler Bridge, and a peak gust of 59 mph was reported at Cape Disappointment.
The Abernathy RAWS measured sustained winds of 44 mph with a peak gust of 64 mph.
There were numerous reports of large trees down on homes and cars in the Kelso, Longview, Columbia Heights, and Lake Sacajawea areas with significant damage.
High winds resulted in downed trees and power outages in the vicinity of Vancouver.
A burst of strong west winds resulted in downed trees along the Columbia River Gorge. A wind gust of 68 mph was measured at Bonneville Dam.
A burst of strong west winds resulted in downed trees along the Columbia River Gorge. A wind gust of 68 mph was measured at Bonneville Dam.

High winds resulted in downed trees and power outages in the vicinity of the Southwest Washington Cascade Foothills. Two near by RAWS (Yellowstone and Eagle Creek) reported wind gusts of 50 mph which is a rare strength for these often wind blocked locations.
Three Corner Rock RAWS measured sustained winds of 72 mph with a peak gust of 94 mph.

Several weather stations along the North Oregon Coast measured high winds with sustained winds between 40 and 45 mph and peak gusts around 59 mph. A power line was blown down from the winds resulting in power outages.
Several weather stations along the Central Oregon coast measured high winds with sustained winds between 40 and 50 mph. The highest recorded wind gust was 67 mph at Gleneden Beach.

A couple of weather stations measured sustained winds of 46 mph with peak gusts between 69 and 71 mph. A 50 ft fir tree was downed and partially snapped. Highway 26 was closed due to downed trees. One tree fell on a car with injuries reported by the media.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: Several weather stations reported high winds in the Central Oregon Coast Range with a peak gust of 67 mph measured at the Rockhouse RAWS. Marys peak measured sustained winds of 59 mph with a peak gust of 83 mph. Official NWS SPotters reported trees and branches down along Highway 36.
Strong winds resulted in several downed trees and power outages in the South Willamette Valley.
Several trees were downed by high winds in the Lower Columbia Valley resulting in significant damage to homes and cars.

High winds caused significant damage in the Portland Metro Area as trees were downed onto homes and cars. Several roads were closed due to downed trees.Marine Drive was closed for several miles due to winds blowing a tractor trailer off of the road. One house caught on fire when a tree downed a electrical wire.
A weather station at Chehalem Ridge reported sustained winds of 46 mph with a peak gust of 60 mph. There were several reports of downed trees and wires with many roads blocked.
Several trees were downed from strong west winds resulting in the closure of I-84 (east bound). A peak gust of 68 mph was measured at the Bonneville Dam.
Several trees were downed from strong west winds resulting in the closure of I-84 (east bound). A peak gust of 68 mph was measured at the Bonneville Dam.

High winds resulted in downed trees and power outages in the vicinity of the Northwest Oregon Cascade Foothills. Two near by RAWS (Yellowstone and Eagle Creek) reported wind gusts of 50 mph which is a rare strength for these often wind blocked locations.
A peak wind gust of 60 mph was measured at the Timberline Lodge, and a peak gust of 58 mph at Government Camp. Ski lifts at the local Ski resorts were suspended due to the strong winds.
The Parkdale Agrimet weather station reported a peak gust of 62 mph.
The weather station at Cape Disappointment measured sustained winds of 44 mph for 22 hours and reported a peak gust of 62 mph during that time.
Heavy rain resulted in urban flooding and several landslides throughout Tillamook County.

The Wilson River near Tillamook, The Trask River near Tillamook, and The Nehalem River near Foss exceeded flood stage. high water from these rivers resulted in the closure of several roads including Highway 101.
Heavy rain resulted in Johnson Creek to exceed major flood stage. Water from the river flooded homes, vehicles, and businesses. Several roads were closed due to the high water.

Heavy rain resulted in urban flooding and small stream flooding throughout the Portland Metro area. The rain was heavy enough to collapse a roof of a business in Gresham Oregon, cause a sink hole near Mt Hood College. High water flowing into Fairview Creek in Gresham snapped a sewage line. Several roads were closed due to high water and the Trimet Max operations were interrupted. water crept into businesses and homes. There were at least two land slides in Portland; one on Corbett Hill, and the other on Cornell Road.
Heavy rain resulted in the Siuslaw River to exceed flood stage at Mapleton. Several small streams also flooded in the area.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding of small streams in the Sweet Home area. Water flooded the basements and lower floors of some homes, and a rock slide closed one lane of Highway 20.

Flooding of Johnson Creek and of the Clackamas River resulted in significant damage to businesses, homes, and vehicles in Milwuakie, Clackamas, Boring, Lake Oswego, and Happy Valley. Around 50 homes were evacuated and eight people were rescued. High water and debris flow closed several roads in the area.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding of the Siltez river near Siletz and the Alsea River near Tidewater. High water covered many roads.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding of the Lukiamute River near Suver as well as several streams in the area. Water covered many of the roads including the closure of Highway 18.

Heavy rain resulted in flooding of the Tualatin River near Dilly, and of many small creeks between Beaverton and Gaston. Around 50 homes sustained flood damage and many roads were closed including Highway 217 in Beaverton (during the evening commute).
Heavy rain resulted in urban flooding in McMinnville with standing water reported in town. High water closed several roads in the area including Highway 99.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding of the Nehalem River near Vernonia, and several small streams in the area. The Timber Road Bridge over Gales Creek washed out north of Highway 6.
Heavy rain resulted in the flooding of Hood River near Hood River.

Heavy rain resulted in urban flooding across the Vancouver metro area. SE Mill PLain was closed between 172nd and 192nd due to deep standing water. An apartment building in Hazell Dell was evacuated due to a land slide.
Heavy rain resulted in small stream flooding and land slides across Skamania County.

Anomalous high tides and large surf prevented flooded rivers to recede between rain events on December 7th and 8th, and contributed to coastal flooding across Tillamook County. The Nehalem River near Foss and the Wilson River near Tillamook crested above major flood stage. The Track river near Tillamook exceeded flood stage. Several homes and roads were flooded included highway 101 and highway 22. Miami Foley Rd in Garibaldi was also closed. Heavy rain also resulted in several land slides in the area. A Fish Hatchery was over topped in Tillamook county with minimal fish loss.

Heavy rain resulted in urban flooding across the Portland metro area. All Amtrack and freight trains were shut down between Portland and Vancouver due to flooding. A mobile home park in Gresham flooded. There were a couple of land slides on Highway 30 where debris covered the highway. One of these slides was near German Town Road. The other slide was near the St John's Bridge, hit a car (with no injuries) as it happened, and covered all lanes of Highway 30.

Flooding from the Nehalem River and Rock Creek in Vernonia resulted in evacuation of homes and the implementation of the Vernonia Emergency Command Center. Heavy rain resulted in a land slide that closed OR47 at mile marker 8.
The Oregon State route 22 was closed due to erosion (sinkhole) from heavy rain. Oregon state route 153 was closed due to high water on the roads between mile markers 1 and 6.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding of the Lukiamute River near Suver.

The Cowlitz River at Kelso exceeded flood stage. Rises of the Kalama River resulted in flood damage of many businesses in Kalama including Motel 6, Remax, and the Burger Bar. Camp Kalama was closed due to flooding of the Kalama River. The I-5 offramp in Longview was closed due to high water.

Heavy rain resulted in multiple land slides between Longview and Kalama. Highway 30 and Kalama River Road were closed due to multiple slides and stranded some residents. A land slide hit a residence and trapped the owner with no injuries.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding of the Grays River near Rosburg.

The Nehalem River near Vernonia flooded Vernonia resulting in evacuation of residents and damage to many buildings and vehicles. A bridge washed out on TImber Road and isolated the Glenwood Community. There was also significant flooding in St Helens, where 17 homes were evacuated, and many roads were damaged and closed. Highway 30 and the business district in Rainier also flooded. An elderly couple drove around a barrier of a closed road, and was swept away by high water. The man escaped through the sunroof of the vehicle, but the woman ended up drowning. Flooding and landslides cut off Western Columbia County.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding of the Tualatin River near Dilley. High water flooded local businesses and residences.
The Cowlitz River flooded near Castle Rock and Kelso. The heavy rain caused a large land slide in Woodland that closed I-5 overnight.

Anomalous high tides and large surf prevented flooded rivers to recede between rain events, and contributed to coastal flooding across the North Oregon coast. Water from high surf entered several rooms of the Surfsand Hotel in Cannon Beach as well as blew out some of the windows. The high surf littered debris on the beach in Neskowin up to the rock barrier. An assisted living facility in Tillamook was evacuated. Highway 101 at Wheeler was closed due to flood damage and a road collapse. Bay Ocean Rd was washed out between Tillamook and Cape Mears.  The port of Columbia River in Astoria was closed as well as the port at Tillamook Bay in Garibaldi. The Nehalem River near Foss remained above flood stage.

Anomalous high tides and large surf prevented flooded rivers to recede between rain events, and contributed to coastal flooding across the Central Oregon coast. A person was briefly trapped in their residence by rising water in Lincoln City. Sewage overflowed into the ocean at Lincoln City. There was some issues with the boat ramps (brows) in Depoe Bay. Heavy rain sank a boat at Depoe Bay. The port at Yaquina Bay in Newport was closed as was the port at Siuslaw River in Florence.
High tides combined with swollen rivers resulted in flooding of many roads in Bay Center, South Bend, and Raymond including parts of Highway 101.
The Tualatin River at West Linn exceeded Flood stage.
The Pudding River at Aurora exceeded flood stage and remained near flood stage for several days (through December 15th).

Heavy rain resulted in new daily rainfall records for the Portland International Airport and downtown Portland. A new daily rainfall of 1.87 inches at the airport broke the previous record of 1.02 inches from 1972. Downtown Portland measures 2.42 inches of rain on the 17th which broke the previous record of 2.26 inches from 1884. Standing water was reported on many roads in the area. The heavy rain caused a landslide on Highway 30 near the St John Bridge.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding of the Mary River near Philomath. There was also a landslide that closed westbound highway 34 near Alsea.

Heavy rain resulted in a multiple of large land slides from Florence to Newport. A landslide in Newport damaged 6 homes and resulted in the evacuation of other near by homes. A car fell into a sink hole in Newport as it opened up a garage. One landslide that struck a home killed an elderly woman and her dog, and injured her husband. A creek near Yachats River Rd pushed a home off of its foundation as it rerouted from the heavy rain. Highway 229 in Siletz flooded. The Siletz River near Siletz and the Alsea River near Tidewater exceeded flood stage. A new daily rainfall record was set in Newport when 3.08 inches of rain on the 17th broke the previous record of 2 inches that was last set in 1925.
High water resulted in the closing of several roads near Tillamook including Highway the Oregon State Route 6 near the Highway 101 intersection.

The Siuslaw River flooded near Mapleton and the Mohawk River flooded near Springfield. Minor flooding of a pastureland was reported in Swisshome due to flooding of Mann Creek. A new daily rainfall record of 1.65 inches in Eugene broke the previous record of 1.35 inches last set in 1957.
The Luckiamute River flooded near Suver.
The Tualatin River flooded near Farmington and Dilley.
The Pudding River flooded near Aurora on the 18th, then remained near flood stage through December 24. The Clackamas River flooded near Estacada on December 18th.

Around 36 homes and 2 businesses sustained damage from the tornado. Dozens of trees with a diameter of 1 to 3 feet were uprooted and blown down, and around a half of a dozen 1 to 2 foot diameter trees were snapped.

A quarter to a half of an inch of ice was observed in portions of the Central Columbia River Gorge as well as several inches of sleet. The ice resulted in power outages, school closures, and slick roads. There was at least one major auto accident on I-84 that closed a couple of lanes on the interstate.

A quarter to a half of an inch of ice was observed in portions of the Western Columbia River Gorge as well as an inch or two of snow or sleet. The ice resulted in power outages, school closures, and slick roads.

A quarter to a half on an inch of ice was observed the the eastern portions of the Portland Metro Area, mainly in Gresham and Troutdale. Tree limbs were broken by the ice and resulted in widespread power outages in eastern Multnomah County.

A quarter to a half of an inch of ice was observed on top of a couple of inches of snow or sleet in the Central Columbia River Gorge. This ice resulted in school closures, slick roads, and power outages.

A quarter to a half of an inch of ice was observed on top of a couple of inches of snow or sleet in areas near the Columbia River Gorge. This ice resulted in school closures, slick roads, and power outages.

A quarter to a half of an inch of ice was observed on top of a couple of inches of snow or sleet in the Western Columbia River Gorge. This ice resulted in school closures, slick roads, and power outages.
Around a quarter of an inch of ice was observed in areas of the South Washington Cascades, mainly in the Wind River Valley.
A quarter of an inch of ice was observed in areas of the Central Columbia River Gorge.
A quarter of an inch of ice was observed in areas of the Central Columbia River Gorge.
Santiam pass observed 15 inches of snow in 24 hours, and Government Camp had 22 inches of new snow.
The Lane County Cascade Foothills observed 4 to 7 inches of snow within 6 hours.
Area SNOTEL's reported 15 to 21 inches of snow within 24 hours over the Lane County Cascades. The greatest snow accumulation was at Roaring River with 21 inches.
A foot of snow was measured in the South Washington Cascades in 12 hours.
A half to a foot of snow fell in the Columbia River Gorge within 12 hours.
There were several reports of 6 to 9 inches of snow within 12 hours for the Upper Hood River Valley.
There were several reports of 6 to 9 inches of snow in the Central Columbia River Gorge within 12 hours.
Several SNOTEL stations measured 18 to 22 inches of snow across the North Oregon Cascades.
Several SNOTEL stations measured between 12 and 18 inches of snow in the Cascades of Lane County.
Several SNOTEL stations measured between 6 and 14 inches of snow in the Northwest Oregon Coast Range.
The Marion Forks SNOTEL measured 16 inches of snow.
A CoCoRahs Observer in Oakridge measured 11 inches of snow.
A couple of SNOTEL sations measured 22 to 26 inches of snow.
Snow observing sites near the Southwest Washington Interior measured 6 to 14 inches of snow. Weather stations within the area reported below freezing temperatures when radar showed frequent showers.
The Calamity SNOTEL measured 18 inches of snow.

Strong winds from a band of thunderstorms brought around 8 large trees down. Some of these trees damaged power poles or took down power lines as they fell, and resulted in power outages. A stop sign was blown down, part of a roof blew off, as well as two chicken coup roofs. Part of a chain link fence form a construction site blew onto 5th Street and blocked the southbound lanes.

Several weather stations along the North Oregon coast reported a brief period of high winds early in the morning. Sustained winds were measured between 40 and 53 mph, and the highest wind gust of 69 mph was reported at Garibaldi.
Two weather stations along the South Washington coast reported a few hours of sustained winds between 49 and 51 mph in the early morning. A peak gust of 61 mph was measured at Cape Disappointment.

One to Two inches of snow fell Jan 3rd followed by 0.10 to 0.20 inch of freezing rain...resulting in very slick driving conditions through Jan 4th. The local news reported several car accidents due to the frozen precipitation on the roads. The City of Portland closed on Monday.
A half to one inch of snow fell followed by 0.10 to 0.15 inch of freezing rain. Slick roads resulted in a lot of traffic accidents and delays.
Around 2 inches of snow fell followed by a trace of freezing rain. Slick roads resulted in traffic delays and accidents.
One to 3 inches of snow fell followed by trace to 0.10 inch of freezing rain. Slick roads resulted in traffic accidents and delays.
One to three inches of snow fell followed by trace to 0.10 inch of freezing rain. Slick roads resulted in traffic delays and accidents.
One to three inches of snow fell followed by trace to 0.10 inch of freezing rain. Slick roads resulted in traffic delays and accidents.
One to 3 inches of snow fell follwed by a trace to 0.10 inch of freezing rain. Slick roads resulted in traffic delays and accidents.
One to three inches of snow followed by a trace to 0.10 inch of freezing rain resulted in traffic accidents and delays.
One to two inches of snow followed by 0.10 to 0.20 inch of freezing rain resulted in traffic accidents and delays.
Sustained winds of 45 mph were measured at several weather stations along the coast, and a peak gust of 59 mph was measured at Garibaldi.
A weather station at Cape Disappointment measured sustained winds of 48 mph with gusts up to 60 mph. Another station on Megler Bridge measured sustained winds of 48 mph.
The Abernathy RAWS measures sustained winds of 36 mph with gusts to 66 mph.
Sustained winds of 42 mph were measured on the Yaquina Bridge in Newport, OR.
A land slide consisting of 100 to 300 cubic yards of soil, rock, and large trees closed  Highway 36 at mile marker 25 for several days.
A peak gust of 58 mph was measured at Ocean Park, and there were sustained winds of 42 mph at Cape Disappointment with a peak gust of 62 mph.
The Abernathy RAWS measured a peak gust of 69 mph. The BPA tower on the Naselle Ridge measured sustained winds of 55 mph with a peak gust of 78 mph.
The Three Corner RAWS measured sustained winds of 47 mph with a peak gust of 79 mph.
Strong winds downed several trees and tree limbs resulting in power outages to several thousand people in Cowlitz County.
Strong winds downed a few trees and tree limbs in Clark County. One tree fell across Highway 503 in Amboy.
Several weather reporting stations along the north Oregon coast measured sustained winds between 40 and 52 mph.
Sustained winds of 47 mph were measured at the Florence/Siuslaw Jetty in the morning with a peak gust of 57 mph. A peak gust of 59 mph was measured in Waldport.
The BPA weather station at Mount Hebo measured a peak gust of 69 mph late in the morning. Other nearby weather stations measured sustained winds of 41 to 52 mph.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The BPA weather station at Marys Peak measured a peak gust of 78 mph, and the Rockhouse RAWS measured sustained winds of 42 mph with a gust up to 64 mph.

Strong winds ahead of the front blew down a weak or dead tree onto a moving vehicle, killing the driver.Winds with the front downed several trees and branches near Beaverton resulting in power outages.
Straight line winds from a thunderstorm blew off a roof from an outbuilding at Ananda Laurelwood Retreat near Gaston.
Thunderstorms and lightning damaged four homes in Nehalem Bay. The homes sustained shingle damage from lightning. One home was heavily damaged with one wall and window blown out.
The ODOT weather station on Megler Bridge in Astoria reported sustained winds of 52 mph.
Sustained winds at Cape Disappointment were 41 mph with a peak gust of 56 mph.
Two stations along the central Oregon coast measured sustained winds between 34 and 43 mph with gusts between 57 and 63 mph.
Several weather reporting stations measured sustained winds between 40 and 61 mph. The highest wind gusy of 79 mph was measured at Cape Disappointment.
The Abernathy RAWS measured sustained winds of 44 mph with a peak gust of 65 mph.
The Three Corner RAWS measured sustained winds of 48 mph with a peak gust of 77 mph.

Many weather reporting stations along the north Oregon coast measured sustained winds between 40 and 60 mph, and several of them had gusts between 73 and 79 mph. The winds downed several large trees, and Pacific Power estimated 22,000 customers along the coast were without power.

Many weather reporting stations along the Central Oregon coast recorded sustained winds between 36 and 48 mph with gusts around 64 mph. The highest wind gust of 74 mph was measured at the Sea Lion Caves.
A couple of weather reporting stations measured wind gusts up to 65 mph. The winds downed several large trees including one that fell onto a moving vehicle resulting in a fatality.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: A couple of weather reporting stations across the central Oregon coast range measured wind gusts between 68 and 79 mph. The winds downed several trees, some which blocked traffic on Highway 18.

A low pressure generated 15 to 35 ft swell with a dominate period of 14 seconds offshore of southwest Washington. This swell generated high surf along the beaches, and resulted in minor damage to the Willapa and Illwaco Ports.

Large waves in Lincoln City caused the water to rise farther up the beach than normal, and knocked an elderly woman off her feet, breaking her leg. The wave also knocked down the injured woman's sister, but she did not sustain any injuries.
Several weather measuring stations along the coast measured sustained winds between 49 and 65 mph. A peak gust of 77 mph was measured at Cape Disappointment.
The Abernathy RAWS measures sustained winds of 36 mph with a peak gust of 64 mph.
Several trees were downed in Clark County by strong winds. One large tree fell onto the train tracks in Ridgefield. An Amtrak train hit the tree and sustained minor damage.
Several weather measuring stations along the coast reported sustained winds between 43 and 47 mph with peak gusts between 55 and 59 mph.
Several weather measuring stations along the coast recorded sustained winds between 41 and 56 mph. A peak gust of 67 mph was measured at Gleneden Beach.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL COAST RANGE OF W OREGON
events.event_narrative: The Rockhouse RAWS measured a peak wind gust of 63 mph.

Strong winds downed several trees in the Portland metro area. Some of these trees fell onto power lines and resulted in power outages, and others fell onto roadways and obstructed traffic. One tree fell onto a home in Portland with minor damage to the roof.
The BPA Tower at Mount Hebo measured a peak gust of 63 mph and the Tidewater RAWS measured a peak gust of 59 mph.
Several SNOTEL stations measured 16 to 24 inches of snow over a 24 to 30 hour period above 3500 feet.
There was 10 to 18 inches of snow measured above 4000 feet.

A county official reported that a 18 to 24 inch diameter tree was snapped by thunderstorm winds near Junction City, and blocked Love Lake Road near milepost 1.75.  The Oregon Department of Transportation reported another tree was downed along the Territorial Highway near milepost 5.
There was a report of 1 inch hail at the baseball field in Welches, Oregon associated with a thunderstorms that moved over the area.
There were several reports and photos of a funnel cloud near Monmouth, Oregon.
A trained spotter observed a funnel cloud along Interstate 5 around 10 miles south of Albany, Oregon.
A trained spotter reported seeing a funnel cloud near Albany, Oregon.
A local media station received several reports of a funnel cloud near the Grotto in northeast Portland.

A young girl was playing on the beach and ended up in deep water. No one witnessed how the girl was swept into the ocean, but it is most likely due to a rip current. She was found 500 feet from the shore and was in the water for around 30 minutes.
Temperatures of 95 to 100 in early June lead to people seeking relief at local rivers. Two river drownings were reported in the Central Willamette Valley during this hot spell.

events.cz_name: CAPE SHOALWATER TO CASCADE HEAD...OUT TO 10 NM
events.event_narrative: A media outlet reported a waterspout just west of Long Beach, WA.
Waterspout just offshore from Cape Disappointment confirmed by U.S. Coast Guard.
Video of a funnel cloud over Rickreall, Oregon was shared over Social Media.
Temperatures of 95 to 100 in early June lead to people seeking relief at local rivers. One drowning was reported east of Springfield during this hot spell.
A funnel cloud was reported by the public near North Plains, OR.
A funnel cloud reported by general public around Canby, OR.
A funnel cloud was observed by a NWS Employee from Interstate 5 near Kalama, Washington.
Temperatures in the upper 80s to mid 90s lead to people seeking relief at local rivers. Two river drownings were reported in the Greater Portland Metro area during this heat event.
Temperatures around 100 degrees lead to people seeking relief at local rivers. One drowning was reported at Paradise Point State Park west of La Center during this hot spell.
Temperatures in the mid 80s to mid 90s lead to people seeking relief at local rivers, lakes, and beaches. One swimmer drowned at Siltcoos Lake south of Florence during this event.
News reported 8 runners were taken to the hospital with heat-related injuries during the Hood-to-Coast relay through Portland.
A woman drowned while swimming along the coast in Long Beach, WA. Her boyfriend who was with her at the time said she was swept out to sea. Thus, her drowning was likely due to a rip current.
Bar Pilot dispatcher reported a brief waterspout in the Columbia River. No damage reported.
Heavy rain with accumulations of 2 to 4 inches along the Coast flooded Highway 6, and left standing water on Highway 101. A landslide occurred blocking Bayocean Road at milepost 2 as well.

NWS Storm Survey Team confirmed a EF-2 Tornado went through Manzanita, with estimated peak winds of 125-130 mph. Tornado started as a waterspout over the Pacific Ocean and came onshore near Treasure Cove Lane and continued northeast through Manzanita.
Video obtained via social media showed a waterspout just offshore of Oceanside along Highway 101. It briefly moved onshore before dissipating. No damage was observed.
Strong thunderstorms produced gusts up to 58 mph, recorded at the ASOS at the Astoria Airport.
The CWOP station at Cape Meares reported gusts up to 79 mph in Tillamook County. A weather station at Garibaldi also recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph.

events.cz_name: CAPE SHOALWATER TO CASCADE HEAD...OUT TO 10 NM
events.event_narrative: Video via social media showed waterspout off the coast of Manzanita move onshore.

events.cz_name: CAPE SHOALWATER TO CASCADE HEAD...OUT TO 10 NM
events.event_narrative: Video obtained via social media showed a waterspout just offshore of Oceanside along Highway 101.
Warrenton Police Department posted a picture to Twitter of 1 to 1.5 inch hail from Hammond, Oregon.
KVAL News reported a landslide blocking the northbound lane of Highway 101 near Yachats.
Heavy rain caused culverts and low-lying urban areas to flood, including 4th and Morrison.  Also flooding was reported at the Portland State University Bookstore.
Weather stations at Clatsop Spit, Tierra Del Mar, and Pacific City all reported peak gusts of 61 mph. Also, in Manzanita, the emergency manager reported a tree fell on an unoccupied truck.

High winds brought down several trees across the area, blocking roads and bringing down power poles and power lines. Wind also caused a grain silo to collapse near Newberg. In Marion County alone, 6600 people lost power as winds downed four feeder lines through Marion County.
Wind brought tree down on Martin Luther King Boulevard near Autzen Stadium.

Weather station at Cape Disappointment recorded a peak gust of 79 mph with sustained winds up to 61 mph. Other stations saw wind gusts up to 62 mph. Washington DOT reported debris on both directions of 101 near the Astoria Megler Bridge.
The Portland Bureau of Transportation reported a landslide blocking SE Malden Street and Southeast Sellwood Blvd.
KGW News shared a video of nuisance flooding in Nehalem during high tide around 12:47 pm PDT.
The Grays River crested at 12.08 feet around 10 am, which is 0.08 feet above flood stage. No damage was reported.
Oregon State University Meteorology Professor reported seeing a funnel cloud looking east of Corvallis.
Flooding in Milwaukie near Fuller Road displaced 7 people from their home. Also, in Gladstone, heavy rain pushed waste water levels to the point that raw sewage leaked into the Clackamas River.

A weather station at Pacific City measured sustained winds of 56 mph with gusts peaking at 69 mph. Other weather stations along the North Oregon Coast recorded sustained winds of 45 to 55 mph with gusts to 65 mph.
The AWOS at the Newport Airport reported max sustained wind at 40 mph with gusts peaking at 59 mph. Another weather station at Yachats reported gusts peaking at 62 mph.

Weather station at Mount Hebo, elevation approximately 3000 feet, recorded wind gusts peaking at 63 mph. In an adjacent zone, the broadcast media also reported a trees down along Chehalem Valley road.  Also, media outlets reported a tree fell over highway 47 near Beaver Creek Trailhead and a vehicle was stuck on the tree.
Reports of downed trees and power lines down, generally on the west side of the Greater Portland Metro Zone. Hillsboro ASOS weather station reported winds gusting up to 37 mph.
